title: Password Reset Requests at the Service Desk
workflow_text:
Notes for covering the password reset queue (Northfield Services help desk)

Most of these come in by phone or the portal. Here's how I handle them:

- Log a ticket first, always, before touching the account. Category = Access > Password Reset.
- Verify the caller. Ask for employee ID + the answer to their security question on file.
  - If they pass, carry on.
  - If they fail, do NOT reset. Tell them to come to the desk in person with their badge, put the ticket on hold, note "ID not verified." (If they get it wrong 3 times in one call, also flag the account to Security - that's the only exception, and it closes our part of it.)
- Once verified, check in the directory whether the account is just expired or actually locked.
  - Expired: send the self-service reset link to their registered mobile.
  - Locked: unlock it first in the admin console, then send the same reset link.
- Stay on the line / wait in chat until they confirm they can log in with the new password.
- Close the ticket with a one-liner on what was done.

That's it - usually under 10 min.
stages: Log a ticket under Access > Password Reset
Verify the caller's identity with employee ID and security question
Check the directory to see if the account is expired or locked
Unlock the account in the admin console (locked accounts only)
Send the self-service reset link to the registered mobile
Wait for the user to confirm they can log in
Close the ticket with a brief summary

decisions.question: Did the caller pass identity verification?
branches: Yes: continue to check the account status
No: do not reset; tell them to come to the desk in person with their badge, put the ticket on hold, and note 'ID not verified'

decisions.question: Is the account expired or locked?
branches: Expired: send the self-service reset link to the registered mobile
Locked: unlock it in the admin console first, then send the reset link

edge_cases: If the caller fails verification 3 times in one call, flag the account to Security in addition to placing the ticket on hold, which ends the help desk's handling.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a caller passes verification and the directory shows their account is locked?
trace_questions.answer: The agent unlocks the account in the admin console, sends the self-service reset link to the registered mobile, waits for the user to confirm they can log in, and then closes the ticket with a brief summary.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a caller fails the security question three times during one call?
trace_questions.answer: No reset is done; the agent tells them to come to the desk in person with their badge, puts the ticket on hold noting 'ID not verified', and also flags the account to Security, which closes the help desk's part of the request.

title: Course Add/Drop Form Processing After the Online Deadline
workflow_text:
Hi Sam - notes for covering the late add/drop inbox while I'm out. This is for students who missed the online add/drop deadline and submit the paper/PDF form instead.

- Forms come into the registrar shared inbox. Log each one in the Late Add/Drop tracker (student ID, course, add or drop, date received).
- Check the form has the instructor's signature. If it's missing, email the student back asking them to get it signed and resubmit. Don't process anything until it comes back. If we haven't heard back in 10 business days, mark it 'Closed - incomplete' in the tracker and stop there.
- Once signed, look at whether it's an add or a drop:
  * ADD -> check seat availability in the SIS. If the section is full, the student needs a capacity override from the department, so forward the form to the dept coordinator and wait for their OK before entering. If there's a seat, just go ahead.
  * DROP -> no seat check needed, go straight to entering it.
- Enter the change in the SIS.
- Email the student a confirmation (use the 'Late Change Confirmed' template) and cc the instructor.
- Mark the tracker row 'Complete'.

That's it - most days there are only a handful. Thanks!
stages: Receive late add/drop form in registrar shared inbox
Log the form in the Late Add/Drop tracker
Verify the instructor's signature on the form
Check seat availability in the SIS (for adds)
Enter the change in the SIS
Email the student a confirmation and cc the instructor
Mark the tracker row 'Complete'

decisions.question: Does the form have the instructor's signature?
branches: Yes: proceed to check whether it is an add or a drop
No: email the student to get it signed and resubmit; hold processing until it returns (close as incomplete after 10 business days with no response)

decisions.question: Is the request an add or a drop?
branches: Add: check seat availability in the SIS; if the section is full, forward to the department coordinator for a capacity override and wait for approval before entering; if a seat is available, enter the change
Drop: skip the seat check and enter the change in the SIS

edge_cases: If a student whose form lacked an instructor signature does not respond within 10 business days, the request is marked 'Closed - incomplete' in the tracker and no further processing occurs.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a signed form requests adding a course whose section is already full?
trace_questions.answer: The form is forwarded to the department coordinator for a capacity override. Staff wait for the coordinator's approval, then enter the change in the SIS, email the student the 'Late Change Confirmed' confirmation with the instructor cc'd, and mark the tracker row 'Complete'.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a drop form arrives without the instructor's signature and the student never replies?
trace_questions.answer: Staff email the student asking them to get it signed and resubmit, and hold processing. After 10 business days with no response, the tracker entry is marked 'Closed - incomplete' and the drop is never entered.

title: Inbound Pallet Receiving at the Distribution Center
workflow_text:
Receiving notes - for whoever covers the dock while I'm out

When a truck shows up, check the driver's paperwork against the open PO list in the warehouse system. If there's no matching PO, don't unload. Call the buyer on the PO contact sheet. If the buyer confirms it's ours (sometimes the PO just hasn't been keyed yet), they'll enter it and you carry on as normal. If the buyer can't confirm it within 30 min, refuse the load. Note the refusal on the driver's BOL and send them off.

Once the PO matches:
- Unload the pallets to the inbound staging lane (lane R1-R4, whichever is open)
- Count cartons and compare to the packing slip
- Look over each pallet for damage (crushed corners, wet boxes, broken wrap)

If counts match and nothing's damaged, sign the BOL clean. If anything is short or damaged, write the exact shortage/damage on the BOL before signing (e.g. "2 ctns short" or "1 plt crushed"), take photos, and email them to claims@ourco-dc. Either way, sign and give the driver their copy.

After that, receive the PO in the system (scan the PO barcode, enter received qty - actual qty, not what the slip says). Print the putaway labels, stick one on each pallet, and move them out of staging so the putaway crew can grab them.

That's it. Don't let pallets sit in R1-R4 past end of shift.
stages: Check driver's paperwork against open PO list
Unload pallets to inbound staging lane
Count cartons against packing slip
Inspect pallets for damage
Sign BOL and give driver their copy
Receive PO in system with actual quantities
Print and apply putaway labels and move pallets out of staging

decisions.question: Does the delivery match an open PO?
branches: Yes: proceed to unload
No: call the buyer to confirm whether the load is ours

decisions.question: Do the carton counts match and is everything undamaged?
branches: Yes: sign the BOL clean
No: note exact shortage/damage on the BOL, take photos, email claims, then sign

edge_cases: No matching PO: buyer is called; if buyer confirms, they enter the PO and receiving continues normally; if not confirmed within 30 minutes, the load is refused, refusal noted on the BOL, and the driver sent away.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a truck arrives with no matching PO and the buyer confirms it is ours after 10 minutes?
trace_questions.answer: The buyer enters the PO, and receiving continues normally: unload to staging, count, inspect, sign the BOL, receive in the system, label, and move pallets out of staging.

trace_questions.question: What happens if the PO matches but the count is 2 cartons short and one pallet is crushed?
trace_questions.answer: The receiver writes the exact shortage and damage on the BOL, takes photos, emails them to claims, signs the BOL and gives the driver a copy, then receives the PO in the system using the actual quantity received, and labels and moves the pallets out of staging.

title: Debit Card Replacement Request at Branch Counter
workflow_text:
Card replacement – counter notes (for new tellers at Riverside Community Bank)

When a customer comes in asking for a replacement debit card:

- First verify ID. Need govt photo ID + confirm last 4 of SSN against the profile. If the ID doesn't match the account holder, stop, don't discuss the account, and refer them to the branch manager.
- Ask why they need a new card. If it's LOST or STOLEN -> block the old card in CardDesk right away (status 'Hot'). If it's just damaged/worn, leave the old card active until the new one is activated, and have them cut up the old one in front of you.
- Check the address on file w/ the customer. Update if needed before ordering, otherwise the card ships to the old address.
- Order the replacement in CardDesk. Standard mail = no fee. Rush is $25 and only if the customer asks for it.
- Give the customer the printed confirmation slip (has the order # and est. delivery date).
- Log the request in the daily service log with the reason code.

Note: if CardDesk throws an error when you try to place the order (happens sometimes in the morning), wait a few min and retry. If it fails 3 times, fill out a paper Card Request Form and leave it in the ops tray. Ops will key it in by end of day. Still give the customer a copy of the paper form instead of the slip.
stages: Verify customer identity with photo ID and last 4 of SSN
Ask the customer the reason for replacement
Block the old card or keep it active and destroy it, depending on the reason
Confirm and update the mailing address on file
Order the replacement card in CardDesk (standard or rush)
Give the customer the printed confirmation slip
Log the request in the daily service log with reason code

decisions.question: Does the ID match the account holder?
branches: Yes: continue with the replacement request
No: stop, do not discuss the account, and refer to the branch manager

decisions.question: Is the card lost/stolen or just damaged/worn?
branches: Lost or stolen: immediately block the old card in CardDesk (status 'Hot')
Damaged/worn: leave old card active until new one is activated and have customer cut up the old card in front of the teller

edge_cases: If CardDesk errors when placing the order, wait a few minutes and retry; after 3 failures, complete a paper Card Request Form, leave it in the ops tray for ops to key in by end of day, and give the customer a copy of the paper form instead of the confirmation slip.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a customer with valid matching ID reports their card stolen, and CardDesk fails three times when the teller tries to order the replacement?
trace_questions.answer: The teller blocks the old card in CardDesk (status 'Hot'), confirms the address, then after three failed order attempts fills out a paper Card Request Form, leaves it in the ops tray for ops to enter by end of day, gives the customer a copy of the paper form instead of the confirmation slip, and logs the request in the daily service log.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a customer's card is worn out and their ID matches, but they have moved since opening the account?
trace_questions.answer: The old card stays active until the new one is activated and the customer cuts it up in front of the teller; the teller updates the address on file before ordering the replacement (standard mail at no fee unless they request $25 rush), gives the confirmation slip, and logs the request.

title: Outpatient Clinic Prescription Refill Requests
workflow_text:
Refill requests – how we handle them at Maplewood Family Clinic (for new front desk/nursing staff)

Requests come in via the patient portal or the refill phone line. Whoever picks it up:

- Log the request in the refill queue (pt name, DOB, med, dose, pharmacy).
- Pull up the chart and check when the pt was last seen by their provider.

If last visit was within 12 months -> send straight to the nurse refill pool. If it's been more than 12 months, don't send it to nursing. Call the pt and book a follow-up appt instead. We can authorize ONE 30-day bridge supply so they don't run out before the appt, but that still goes through the nurse pool like a normal refill.

Nurse pool:
- RN reviews the med against the clinic refill protocol.
- Routine meds on protocol (BP meds, statins, etc.) -> RN approves and e-sends to pharmacy.
- Controlled substances or anything not on protocol -> RN routes to the prescribing provider's inbox for sign-off. Provider approves/denies and e-sends if approved.

After it's sent (or denied), send the pt a portal message or call to let them know the outcome, then close the request in the queue.

Note: provider inbox items should be handled within 2 business days. If one is still sitting there after 2 days (provider out, etc.), RN escalates to the covering provider for that day.
stages: Log the refill request in the refill queue
Check the patient's last visit date in the chart
Send the request to the nurse refill pool
RN reviews the medication against the refill protocol
Approve and e-send the prescription to the pharmacy (by RN or provider)
Notify the patient of the outcome
Close the request in the queue

decisions.question: Was the patient seen by their provider within the last 12 months?
branches: Yes: send the request straight to the nurse refill pool.
No: call the patient to book a follow-up appointment; a single 30-day bridge supply may be authorized, which still goes through the nurse pool.

decisions.question: Is the medication a routine med on the clinic refill protocol?
branches: Yes: RN approves and e-sends to the pharmacy.
No (controlled substance or not on protocol): RN routes to the prescribing provider's inbox; the provider approves and e-sends, or denies.

edge_cases: If a request sits in the provider's inbox for more than 2 business days (e.g., provider is out), the RN escalates it to that day's covering provider.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a patient last seen 18 months ago requests a refill of their blood pressure medication?
trace_questions.answer: Staff do not send a regular refill; they call the patient to book a follow-up appointment. A single 30-day bridge supply can be authorized, which goes through the nurse pool; since a BP med is on protocol, the RN approves and e-sends it. The patient is then notified and the request closed.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a patient seen 3 months ago requests a controlled substance refill and the prescribing provider is out of office for a week?
trace_questions.answer: The request goes to the nurse pool, and because it is a controlled substance the RN routes it to the prescribing provider's inbox. After it sits there for 2 business days, the RN escalates it to the covering provider, who approves (and e-sends) or denies it; the patient is then notified and the request closed.

title: New Hire Equipment Request Processing
workflow_text:
Hi Sam - quick notes on how we handle laptop/equipment requests for new hires while I'm out.

- Hiring manager submits the New Hire Equipment form in the HR portal, usually 2 weeks before start date. First thing: check the form is complete (start date, role, dept, cost center). If anything's missing, send it back to the manager and wait for the resubmit - don't start anything until it's complete.
- Once it's complete, look up the role in the Standard Kit sheet to see what they get.

Standard vs non-standard:
- If the request matches the standard kit for that role, just go ahead and create the order ticket with IT Ops.
- If the manager asked for anything extra (2nd monitor, higher spec laptop, etc.), it needs dept head sign-off first. Email the dept head with the request. If they approve, create the IT ticket with the extras included. If they decline, create the ticket with the standard kit only and let the manager know the extras were declined.

After the ticket's in:
- Log the ticket number on the new hire's onboarding checklist in the HRIS.
- IT Ops confirms when the kit's been imaged and ready. When you get that, book a pickup/setup slot for the new hire's first day and email the details to the manager.
- Mark the equipment item as done on the checklist.

Heads up: dept heads sometimes sit on approvals. If you haven't heard back in 3 business days, don't keep waiting - send the standard kit ticket so the person isn't without a laptop on day 1, and tell the manager the extras can be requested separately later.

Thanks!
Priya, HR Ops

Check form for completeness
Look up role in Standard Kit sheet
Create order ticket with IT Ops
Log ticket number on new hire's onboarding checklist in HRIS
Receive IT Ops confirmation that kit is ready
Book first-day pickup/setup slot and email details to manager
Mark equipment item as done on checklist

branches: Yes: proceed to look up the role in the Standard Kit sheet
No: send it back to the manager and wait for resubmission before starting anything

decisions.question: Does the request include anything beyond the standard kit for the role?
branches: No (standard only): create the IT Ops order ticket directly

Yes (extras requested): email the dept head for sign-off; if approved, create the ticket including extras; if declined, create the ticket with standard kit only and tell the manager the extras were declined

edge_cases: Dept head does not respond to an extras approval request within 3 business days: submit the standard kit ticket anyway so the new hire has a laptop on day 1, and tell the manager the extras can be requested separately later.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a complete form requests a second monitor and the dept head declines it?
trace_questions.answer: An IT Ops ticket is created with the standard kit only, and the manager is told the extras were declined. The ticket number is then logged on the HRIS checklist, and once IT confirms the kit is ready, a first-day setup slot is booked, the details are emailed to the manager, and the item is marked done.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a form is missing the cost center and, once resubmitted, requests a higher-spec laptop but the dept head never replies?
trace_questions.answer: The form is sent back to the manager, and nothing starts until it is resubmitted complete. After that, the dept head is emailed for approval of the extra. With no reply in 3 business days, the standard kit ticket is submitted and the manager is told the extras can be requested separately later. The process then continues with logging the ticket, waiting for IT's confirmation, booking the setup slot, and marking the item done.

title: Tuition Reimbursement Request Processing
workflow_text:
Tuition reimb - notes for Dana while I'm on leave

Requests come in through the TR-1 pre-approval form (shared inbox, subject line usually says "tuition"). The form is supposed to be in BEFORE the course start date.
- If the start date has already passed, don't process it normally. Forward it to the HR Director, who decides whether to grant an exception. If she says no, send the late-submission decline (template in the TR folder). If she grants the exception, carry on as usual from the eligibility check.

Eligibility check: pull them up in the HRIS.
- Need 6+ months tenure AND not currently on a PIP.
- If either one fails, send the "not eligible" decline template and mark the row Closed - Ineligible in the tracker. That's the end.

If they're eligible, email the TR-1 to their direct manager for job-relatedness sign-off. The manager just replies approve/decline.
- Decline -> forward the manager's reason to the employee and close the request as Closed - Mgr Declined.
- Approve -> add it to the tracker as Active and send the approval letter. The letter states the annual cap ($5,250/calendar yr) and reminds them we need the grade + receipt within 30 days of the course ending.
- Managers sit on these sometimes. If there's no answer in 5 business days, send one reminder. Still nothing 3 business days after that? Escalate to the manager's director, who can approve or decline in the manager's place.

After the course: the employee sends the final grade report + itemized receipt (tuition and required fees only, no parking/books).
- Grade has to be B or better (or "Pass" for pass/fail courses).
- Below that = no reimbursement. Email the employee that the grade doesn't meet the minimum and close as Closed - Grade.

If the grade is OK, work out the amount: eligible costs, but no more than what's left of their $5,250 for the year (check YTD paid in the tracker, since some people take 2-3 courses). If they've only got part of the cap left, pay up to the remainder.

Send the amount to payroll on the reimbursement sheet by Wed to hit the next cycle. Once payroll confirms, let the employee know the amount + pay date and mark it Closed - Paid. Update YTD.
stages: Receive TR-1 pre-approval form from employee
Check eligibility in HRIS (tenure and PIP status)
Send TR-1 to direct manager for job-relatedness sign-off
Log request as Active in tracker and send approval letter
Collect final grade report and itemized receipt after course ends
Verify grade meets minimum
Calculate reimbursement amount against remaining annual cap
Submit amount to payroll on reimbursement sheet
Notify employee of amount and pay date, close as Paid, and update YTD

decisions.question: Is the employee eligible (6+ months tenure and not on a PIP)?
branches: Yes: send the TR-1 to the direct manager for sign-off
No: send the 'not eligible' decline template and close as Closed - Ineligible

decisions.question: Does the manager approve the course as job-related?
branches: Approve: log as Active in tracker and send approval letter
Decline: forward manager's reason to employee and close as Closed - Mgr Declined

decisions.question: Is the grade B or better (or Pass for pass/fail)?
branches: Yes: calculate reimbursement amount
No: email employee that grade doesn't meet minimum and close as Closed - Grade, no reimbursement

edge_cases: Form submitted after course start date: forwarded to HR Director for an exception; if denied, send late-submission decline; if granted, continue from the eligibility check
Manager does not respond: send one reminder after 5 business days; if still no answer 3 business days later, escalate to the manager's director, who approves or declines in the manager's place
Employee has only part of the $5,250 annual cap remaining: reimburse only up to the remaining amount

trace_questions.question: What happens if an eligible employee's request is approved by their manager, but they finish the course with a C grade?
trace_questions.answer: No reimbursement is paid. HR emails the employee that the grade does not meet the minimum (B or better/Pass) and closes the request in the tracker as Closed - Grade; nothing is sent to payroll.

trace_questions.question: What happens if an employee submits the TR-1 after the course has started, the HR Director grants an exception, but the employee is currently on a PIP?
trace_questions.answer: After the exception the request continues to the eligibility check, which it fails because the employee is on a PIP. HR sends the 'not eligible' decline template and marks the request Closed - Ineligible; it never goes to the manager.

title: Replenishment PO for Low-Stock SKUs
workflow_text:
Replenishment PO process (covering for Dana while she's out)

Every Monday AM pull the Reorder Point report from the ERP (Inventory > Reports > Below ROP). Anything listed there is at or under its reorder point.

Before you cut a PO for a SKU, look at the open PO tab for it. If there's already an open PO whose qty covers the gap back up to max stock, don't place another one. Just add a note on the report line ("covered by PO #___") and move on. Double ordering has burned us before.

If it's not covered:
- Build the PO in the ERP using the preferred supplier on the Approved Vendor List. Qty = max stock minus (on hand + any partial open qty). Use the AVL price. Don't type one in by hand.
- Need date = today + the SKU's standard lead time, unless the report shows it's already at zero. Then put the need date as ASAP and flag it.
- PO total over $10,000 → it routes to Marcus (ops manager) for approval before it can be released. Under $10k you can release it yourself.
  - If Marcus is out, the approval goes to the ops director instead. Don't sit on it waiting for him.

Release/email the PO to the supplier's order desk (address is on the AVL).

Supplier should send an order acknowledgment w/ confirmed ship date within 2 business days. If nothing by then, send a follow-up email. Still nothing 1 business day after the follow-up → call them, and if you can't get a confirmed date on the call, cancel the PO and re-place it with the backup supplier on the AVL (start over from building the PO, approval rules still apply).

Once you have the ack, compare the confirmed ship date to the need date.
- Within 5 business days of need date: fine, accept.
- More than 5 business days late: ask the supplier to expedite. If they agree, use the new date. If they say no, accept their date anyway but put the SKU on the shortage watch list and give sales ops a heads up.

Enter the confirmed ship date + tracking/ETA on the PO line in the ERP so the system shows the right expected receipt.

Then send the weekly inbound list to receiving so they can plan dock slots.

Save the ack PDF to the PO folder on the shared drive. Done.
stages: Pull the weekly Below Reorder Point report from the ERP
Check open POs for each listed SKU to see whether the shortfall is already covered
Build the PO with the preferred supplier from the Approved Vendor List, calculating quantity and need date
Obtain approval from the ops manager when required
Release/email the PO to the supplier's order desk
Obtain the supplier's order acknowledgment with a confirmed ship date
Compare the confirmed ship date to the need date
Enter the confirmed ship date and ETA on the PO line in the ERP
Send the inbound list to receiving for dock planning
Save the acknowledgment PDF to the PO folder on the shared drive

decisions.question: Does an existing open PO already cover the gap back up to max stock?
branches: Yes: do not place a new PO; note the covering PO number on the report line and move on
No: build a new PO with the preferred supplier

decisions.question: Is the PO total over $10,000?
branches: Yes: route to Marcus (ops manager) for approval before release (or to the ops director if Marcus is out)
No: the planner releases the PO directly

decisions.question: Is the confirmed ship date more than 5 business days later than the need date?
branches: No (within 5 business days): accept the date
Yes: ask the supplier to expedite; if they agree, use the new date; if they refuse, accept their date, add the SKU to the shortage watch list, and notify sales ops

edge_cases: No acknowledgment within 2 business days: send a follow-up email; if still nothing 1 business day later, call the supplier; if no confirmed date is obtained on the call, cancel the PO and re-place it with the backup supplier, restarting from PO creation with the same approval rules
Ops manager unavailable for a PO over $10,000: approval goes to the ops director instead of waiting

trace_questions.question: What happens if a $14,500 PO is released and the supplier sends no acknowledgment within 2 business days, ignores the follow-up email, and can't give a confirmed date when called?
trace_questions.answer: The PO is cancelled and re-placed with the backup supplier on the Approved Vendor List. The process restarts from building the PO, and because the total is still over $10,000 it must again be approved by Marcus (or the ops director if he is out) before release.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a $6,000 PO is acknowledged with a ship date 8 business days after the need date and the supplier refuses to expedite?
trace_questions.answer: The planner released the PO without approval since it's under $10,000. Because the date is more than 5 business days late, the planner asks for an expedite; when the supplier refuses, the planner accepts the supplier's date, adds the SKU to the shortage watch list, and notifies sales ops, then enters the confirmed date in the ERP, includes it on the inbound list to receiving, and files the ack.

title: Outgoing Domestic Wire Transfer Request at Branch
workflow_text:
Outgoing domestic wires: counter notes for new tellers (Riverside branch)

Customer wants to send a wire. Hand them the WR-2 form and have them fill in beneficiary name, beneficiary acct #, routing #, beneficiary bank name, amount, and purpose. Check every field before you go further. Blank routing # = hand it back.

Check their ID against the signer list on the account. If they're not a listed signer, we can't take it. Politely stop there and tell them the account owner has to come in. Don't start the form in the system.

Pull the acct up in CoreView. Available bal has to cover the amount PLUS the $25 wire fee. If it doesn't:
- tell the cust the shortfall
- they can move money from another acct they have with us right then, then pick back up
- or they come back another day
- do NOT send a partial wire

Approval depends on amount:
* under $10,000: you approve it yourself. Initial the approval box on the WR-2.
* $10,000 and up: flag it in the Ops queue for callback verification. Ops calls the customer at the phone # ON FILE, never a number the customer gives you today. You wait for Ops to mark it verified before you go on.
  - If Ops can't reach them within 2 hrs, they leave a msg and the wire sits until the next business day. If there's still no contact by end of that next day, Ops cancels the request and mails the customer a letter. Nothing gets debited in that case.

Once it's approved or verified, key it into WireLink and hit Submit. Submit is what debits the acct for amount + fee, so don't submit early. Cutoff is 3:00 pm. Anything submitted after 3 goes out the next business day. Make sure you tell the customer if that applies.

Print the confirmation (has the wire ref #). Cust gets a copy. Branch copy plus the WR-2 go in the wire binder.
stages: Have customer complete the WR-2 wire request form and check all fields
Verify customer ID against the account signer list
Confirm available balance covers wire amount plus $25 fee
Approve wire (teller initials) or flag it for Ops callback verification
Ops calls customer at phone number on file to verify (for $10,000+)
Enter wire into WireLink and submit (debits account for amount plus fee)
Inform customer of send date if submitted after 3:00 pm cutoff
Print confirmation with wire reference number
Give customer a copy and file branch copy with WR-2 in the wire binder

decisions.question: Is the customer a listed signer on the account?
branches: Yes: continue to balance check
No: stop the request and tell the customer the account owner must come in

decisions.question: Does the available balance cover the wire amount plus the $25 fee?
branches: Yes: proceed to approval
No: tell customer the shortfall. They may transfer funds from another account at the bank and continue, or return another day. No partial wire is sent.

decisions.question: Is the wire amount under $10,000?
branches: Yes (under $10,000): teller approves by initialing the WR-2
No ($10,000 or more): flag for Ops callback verification to phone number on file before proceeding

edge_cases: Callback cannot be completed: if Ops cannot reach the customer within 2 hours, they leave a message and the wire waits until the next business day. If there is still no contact by end of that day, Ops cancels the request and mails the customer a letter, and the account is not debited.
After-cutoff submission: wires submitted in WireLink after 3:00 pm go out the next business day, and the customer must be told.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a listed signer with sufficient funds requests a $15,000 wire, and Ops cannot reach them at the number on file that day or by the end of the next business day?
trace_questions.answer: The wire is flagged for Ops callback. After 2 hours with no contact, Ops leaves a message and the wire waits until the next business day. With still no contact by end of that day, Ops cancels the request and mails the customer a letter. The wire is never submitted, so the account is not debited.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a listed signer with enough balance to cover the amount plus fee requests a $4,000 wire and the teller submits it at 3:30 pm?
trace_questions.answer: The teller approves it by initialing the WR-2, since it is under $10,000. Submitting it in WireLink debits the account for $4,025. Because it is after the 3:00 pm cutoff, it goes out the next business day, and the teller tells the customer. The confirmation is printed, the customer gets a copy, and the branch copy and WR-2 are filed in the wire binder.

title: Cardiology Clinic New Patient Referral Intake
workflow_text:
Referral intake notes (Cardiology, Lakeside Specialty Group) for whoever is covering the front desk queue while I'm out.

New referrals come in through the e-referral portal and the fax inbox. Check both at least twice a day (AM + after lunch). Pull every new one and get it into the referral tracker before you do anything else, because the 'days open' clock runs from the tracker date.

First look at the packet itself. We need:
- pt demographics + phone that works
- insurance (front/back of card or member ID at minimum)
- reason for referral / dx
- last office note from referring provider (within 90 days)
- any recent EKG or echo if they mention one

If anything's missing, send the referring office the 'Incomplete Referral' request through the portal (or fax if that's how it came in) and set the tracker status to HOLD-INFO. Give them 3 business days. No answer, send a second request and call their referral coordinator. If we still have nothing 2 business days after that, close it out: status CLOSED-INCOMPLETE and fax the closure letter to the referring provider so they know. Don't let these sit forever, they mess up our backlog numbers.

Once the packet is complete, run eligibility in the payer portal. Some plans (mostly the HMO ones, check the payer grid on the shared drive) need a prior auth before a new specialist visit.
- Auth needed → submit it through the payer portal with the office note attached, status AUTH-PENDING. Keep in mind triage below; if the nurse marks it urgent, go back in and request expedited review.
- If the payer denies, don't schedule. Send the denial back to the referring office so they can appeal or redirect; status CLOSED-DENIED.
- No auth needed → move straight on.

Then it goes to the triage nurse bucket (don't wait on auth for this part, triage can happen while auth is pending). Nurse reads the notes and marks URGENT or ROUTINE.
- URGENT: pt needs to be seen within 7 days. Call the pt same day to book. Use the held urgent slots on the schedule.
- ROUTINE: next available new-pt slot. Call pt to book, or send a portal message if they're on the portal.

If auth was required, you can only book once it's approved.

Scheduling calls: 3 attempts on different days. If we can't reach them after the 3rd, mail the 'Unable to Reach' letter and notify the referring office, status CLOSED-NO-CONTACT. For urgent ones do all 3 attempts within 2 days and let the triage nurse know after the 2nd miss.

After they're booked: fax/portal the appt confirmation to the referring office, and send the pt the new-patient packet (forms, med list sheet, directions). Status SCHEDULED. Done.
stages: Pull new referrals from the e-referral portal and fax inbox
Log the referral in the referral tracker
Review the referral packet for completeness
Verify insurance eligibility in the payer portal
Submit prior authorization to the payer when required
Route the referral to the triage nurse for urgency review
Contact the patient to schedule the appointment
Send appointment confirmation to the referring office
Send the new-patient packet to the patient and mark status SCHEDULED

decisions.question: Is the referral packet complete (demographics, insurance, reason, recent office note, relevant tests)?
branches: Yes: proceed to insurance eligibility check
No: send Incomplete Referral request, set HOLD-INFO, wait 3 business days, then second request + call; close as CLOSED-INCOMPLETE if nothing 2 business days later

decisions.question: Does the patient's plan require prior authorization for a new specialist visit?
branches: Yes: submit auth (expedited if triaged urgent), status AUTH-PENDING; if approved, booking can proceed; if denied, send denial to referring office and close as CLOSED-DENIED
No: proceed directly to triage and scheduling

decisions.question: Does the triage nurse classify the referral as urgent or routine?
branches: URGENT: call patient same day, book within 7 days using held urgent slots, make all 3 contact attempts within 2 days and notify nurse after 2nd miss
ROUTINE: book next available new-patient slot by phone or portal message

edge_cases: Referring office does not respond to missing-information requests: after the 3-business-day hold, a second request and a call, the referral is closed as CLOSED-INCOMPLETE 2 business days later and a closure letter is faxed to the referring provider.

Patient cannot be reached after 3 scheduling attempts on different days: mail the Unable to Reach letter, notify the referring office, and set status CLOSED-NO-CONTACT (for urgent referrals the attempts are compressed into 2 days and the triage nurse is alerted after the 2nd miss).
Prior authorization is denied: the patient is not scheduled, the denial goes back to the referring office, and the referral is closed as CLOSED-DENIED.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a referral arrives without the patient's insurance information and the referring office never responds?
trace_questions.answer: The referral is logged, an Incomplete Referral request is sent and status set to HOLD-INFO. After 3 business days with no answer, a second request is sent and the office's referral coordinator is called. If still nothing after 2 more business days, the referral is closed as CLOSED-INCOMPLETE and a closure letter is faxed to the referring provider.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a complete referral is for a patient whose HMO plan requires prior authorization and the triage nurse marks it URGENT?
trace_questions.answer: After eligibility is checked, auth is submitted (status AUTH-PENDING) and triage proceeds in parallel; once marked urgent, staff go back and request expedited review. The appointment can only be booked once auth is approved; then the patient is called to book within 7 days using held urgent slots, with all 3 contact attempts within 2 days if needed. After booking, the confirmation goes to the referring office and the new-patient packet to the patient, status SCHEDULED. If auth is denied, the patient is not scheduled and the denial goes to the referring office (CLOSED-DENIED).

title: Extended Leave of Absence Request Processing
workflow_text:
Leave of absence (LOA) handling: notes for whoever's covering the leave queue while I'm out

Requests come into the HR leave inbox as the LOA form. First, log it in the case tracker so the clock starts. Then pull the employee up in the HRIS and check tenure.

- 12+ months of service = eligible for protected leave. Proceed normally.
- Under 12 months = NOT eligible for protected leave, but don't deny it yourself!! Forward to the HR manager (currently R. Okafor), who decides on discretionary unprotected leave. If she approves, carry on exactly like a normal case, but tick "unprotected" in the tracker. If she says no, send the denial letter template and close the case.

Is it medical (own illness or caring for a family member)? If yes, send the medical certification form to the employee. If it's personal leave (e.g., a sabbatical or relocation), skip certification and go straight to notifying the manager.

Cert review: when it comes back, check that the provider signed it and that it includes dates and the expected duration. If anything is missing, send it back with a note saying what's missing. They can resubmit as many times as needed. BUT the employee has 15 calendar days from when we first sent the form. If that passes with no complete cert, send the provisional denial notice and flag the case to the HR manager. Don't keep chasing.

Once the cert is OK (or skipped for personal leave), email the manager with the leave START/END DATES ONLY. Never forward the cert or the diagnosis to the manager. If a manager asks why, refer them to me or Okafor.

After that, enter the leave in the HRIS with the correct leave code, then send the approval letter to the employee. Do the payroll step before the letter, though: if the leave is over 30 days, payroll needs to set up direct billing for benefit premiums, so email them the dates. For 30 days or less, payroll picks it up from the HRIS code and you don't need to contact them.

The last part of setup is putting a return-to-work check-in on the calendar for the week before the end date.

Extensions: if the employee asks for more time before the end date, treat it like a new medical cert cycle (send form, 15-day window, etc.) and then update the end date in HRIS and re-notify the manager. If they ask after the end date has already passed, it goes to Okafor, not us.

On return: for medical leave, collect the fitness-for-duty clearance from the employee's provider. If it's a full clearance, reactivate them in HRIS and close the case. If it has restrictions, hand it to the HR business partner for an accommodation review before reactivating. They'll tell you when to reactivate. Personal leave doesn't need clearance. Just reactivate and close.
stages: Log LOA request in case tracker
Check employee tenure in HRIS
Send medical certification form to employee
Review returned medical certification
Notify manager of leave start/end dates only
Enter leave in HRIS with correct leave code
Email payroll leave dates for benefit premium billing
Send approval letter to employee
Schedule return-to-work check-in for week before end date
Collect fitness-for-duty clearance on return
Reactivate employee in HRIS and close case

decisions.question: Does the employee have 12 or more months of service?
branches: Yes: eligible for protected leave; proceed normally
No: forward to HR manager for a discretionary leave decision

decisions.question: (Nested, for employees under 12 months) Does the HR manager approve discretionary unprotected leave?
branches: Yes: proceed like a normal case, marked 'unprotected' in tracker
No: send denial letter template and close case

decisions.question: Is the leave medical (own illness or family care)?
branches: Yes: send medical certification form and review it
No (personal leave): skip certification and notify manager directly; no fitness-for-duty clearance needed on return

decisions.question: Is the returned certification complete (provider signature, dates, expected duration)?
branches: Yes: proceed to notify manager
No: send back noting what's missing; employee may resubmit repeatedly within 15 calendar days of the form first being sent

decisions.question: Is the leave longer than 30 days?
branches: Yes: email payroll the dates for direct billing of benefit premiums
No: no payroll contact; payroll uses the HRIS code

decisions.question: Is the fitness-for-duty clearance a full clearance?
branches: Yes: reactivate in HRIS and close case
No (restrictions): HR business partner does accommodation review and says when to reactivate

edge_cases: Certification loop timeout: if there is no complete cert 15 calendar days after the form was first sent, send provisional denial notice, flag to HR manager, and stop chasing

Extension requested before end date: run a new medical cert cycle (form, 15-day window), update end date in HRIS, and re-notify the manager; if requested after end date has passed, route to HR manager
Manager asks for medical details: never share the cert or diagnosis; refer them to HR lead or HR manager

trace_questions.question: What happens if an employee with 8 months of service requests 45 days of medical leave, the HR manager approves it, and the employee returns a complete certification on the second attempt within 15 days?
trace_questions.answer: The case proceeds as normal but is marked 'unprotected' in the tracker. After the complete cert, the manager is notified of dates only, leave is entered in HRIS, payroll is emailed the dates for benefit premium billing (since it's over 30 days), the approval letter is sent, and a return-to-work check-in is scheduled for the week before the end date.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a medical leave employee with 3 years of service returns from leave with a fitness-for-duty clearance that includes restrictions?
trace_questions.answer: They are not reactivated right away. The clearance goes to the HR business partner for an accommodation review, and the employee is reactivated in HRIS and the case closed only when the HR business partner says to.

title: Return-to-Vendor (RTV) for Defective Components
workflow_text:
RTV notes - for whoever is covering while I'm out

Starts when QC flags a bad lot. They put it on QC HOLD in the WMS - if it's not on hold, don't touch anything, ping QC first. Once it's held you get the RTV ticket.

First thing: pull the original PO + the supplier agreement (shared drive > Vendors). You need the PO line, lot #, qty, unit cost. Then email the supplier rep asking for an RMA. Use the RTV template, attach QC's defect report + pics.

If they don't answer in 3 business days -> escalate to their account mgr and resend the request. Clock resets. If it's dead silence again after that 3 days, stop chasing and hand it to the procurement manager, who decides whether we write it off or keep pushing. Lot stays on hold the whole time regardless.

Sometimes they only approve part of the qty on the RMA (happened w/ the connector vendor). Only return what's approved. Whatever's left stays on QC HOLD and you open a separate RTV ticket for it - don't keep it on the original one.

Once you have the RMA #, check what they're giving us:
- credit -> just note the expected credit amt on the ticket for finance
- replacement -> open a replacement PO and link it to the RMA. Check if the part is on the production-critical list. If yes, ask the supplier to expedite and ship the replacement ahead of receiving our return (advance replacement). If not critical, standard lead time is fine.

Warehouse picks the units and stages them in the RTV cage. Don't let them ship yet.

** total RTV value over $2,500 -> photos of the staged units + finance approval BEFORE it leaves. Under that, go ahead.

Freight: if the supplier sends a label / uses their carrier, use that (freight collect). Otherwise we book our own carrier prepaid and bill the freight back to them on the ticket. Either way the RMA # goes on the BOL or they'll refuse it at the dock.

After it ships -> adjust the units out of inventory in the WMS against the RTV ticket.

Then track: credit memo (credit) or replacement receipt (replacement). If a credit hasn't shown up in 30 days from ship date, tell AP to deduct it from the supplier's next invoice. When the credit/replacement is in, close the ticket.
stages: QC places defective lot on hold in WMS
Pull original PO and supplier agreement
Email supplier requesting an RMA
Receive RMA number from supplier
Record expected credit or open linked replacement PO
Pick and stage defective units in RTV cage
Arrange freight (supplier label or own prepaid carrier)
Put RMA number on BOL and ship units
Adjust units out of inventory in WMS
Track credit memo or replacement receipt
Close RTV ticket

decisions.question: Did the supplier respond to the RMA request within 3 business days?
branches: Yes: proceed with the RMA
No (first time): escalate to supplier's account manager and resend; clock resets
No again after escalation: hand to procurement manager to decide write-off or keep pushing; lot stays on hold

decisions.question: Is the supplier issuing a credit or a replacement?
branches: Credit: note expected credit amount on the ticket for finance
Replacement: open replacement PO linked to the RMA, then check production-critical status

decisions.question: (Nested under replacement) Is the part on the production-critical list?
branches: Yes: ask supplier to expedite and ship an advance replacement before receiving our return
No: standard lead time

decisions.question: Is the total RTV value over $2,500?
branches: Yes: photograph staged units and get finance approval before shipping
No: ship without extra approval

decisions.question: Did the supplier provide a label/carrier?
branches: Yes: use supplier's carrier, freight collect
No: book own carrier prepaid and bill freight back to supplier on the ticket

edge_cases: Supplier non-response loop: escalate once to account manager and resend; if still no response in 3 business days, procurement manager decides write-off vs. keep pushing, with lot on hold throughout.
Partial RMA approval: only approved quantity is returned; remaining units stay on QC hold under a separate new RTV ticket.
Credit not received within 30 days of ship date: AP deducts the amount from the supplier's next invoice.

trace_questions.question: What happens if the supplier doesn't answer the RMA request in 3 business days, and also doesn't answer within 3 business days after the request is escalated to their account manager?
trace_questions.answer: The buyer stops chasing and hands the case to the procurement manager, who decides whether to write it off or keep pushing; the lot remains on QC hold the whole time.

trace_questions.question: What happens if the supplier approves a replacement for a production-critical part and the staged return is worth $4,000?
trace_questions.answer: The buyer opens a replacement PO linked to the RMA and asks the supplier to expedite an advance replacement shipped before our return arrives; after staging in the RTV cage, the units must be photographed and finance must approve before they ship, with the RMA number on the BOL.

title: Outpatient MRI Prior Authorization Processing
workflow_text:
MRI prior auth notes (covering for Dana while she's out, read the whole thing first)

Orders come into the Imaging Auth work queue in the EHR. Grab the oldest first unless something is flagged URGENT (see bottom).

Before anything else, run eligibility. If coverage comes back inactive or termed, DON'T start an auth. Route to Financial Counseling and they'll do a self-pay estimate with the patient. If the patient says ok to self-pay, FC sends it back to us, and we just mark it self-pay and release to scheduling, no auth needed. If the patient declines, FC cancels the order and lets the ordering provider know. Either way we're done with that one.

Active coverage -> look up the CPT on that payer's auth-required list (binder + payer portal, portal wins if they disagree). Some plans don't need auth for certain MRIs. If no auth needed, still call the payer to confirm, put the call ref # in the order note, and release to scheduling.

If auth IS required:
- pull clinical docs: last office note, imaging hx, and for lumbar/cervical spine the payer almost always wants 6 wks of conservative tx documented (PT, meds, etc.)
- if docs are thin, send an in-basket msg to the ordering provider asking for an addendum. Order sits on hold. Give them 3 business days. No response by then -> escalate to the clinic manager, who'll chase the provider. Don't submit with incomplete docs, it just gets denied.
- once docs are good, submit through the payer portal
- log the reference # in the Auth Tracker spreadsheet right away

Then it's waiting. Check the tracker every business day for pendings. Payer comes back one of three ways:
* Approved: put the auth # and valid date range in the order, release to scheduling.
* Needs more info: get what they asked for (usually from the provider again), resubmit under the same ref #, and go back to checking daily. This can bounce more than once, that's normal.
* Denied: send the denial letter to the ordering provider. Provider decides if they want a peer-to-peer. If yes, we book the P2P (has to happen within 14 days of the denial or the payer won't do it). If the P2P overturns it, treat it like an approval. If the P2P upholds the denial, or if the provider didn't want a P2P at all, provider picks: written appeal (we put the packet together and hand it to the Appeals team) or cancel the order. If cancelled we call the patient and close it out.

Scheduling books inside the auth date range, and the patient gets a confirmation call w/ appt + prep instructions. That's the end for us.

Oh, things that trip people up:
- if the scan date gets pushed past the auth end date (pt reschedules, machine down, whatever), scheduling kicks it back and we have to request an extension from the payer BEFORE the old auth expires. If it already expired, it's a brand new submission.
- URGENT/stat orders: don't hold the scan for auth. Scan goes ahead, and we submit a retro auth within 2 business days of the scan date. Same docs, same tracker.
stages: Pull order from Imaging Auth work queue
Run insurance eligibility check
Look up CPT code on payer's auth-required list
Gather clinical documentation from the chart
Request provider addendum for missing documentation
Submit auth request through payer portal
Log reference number in Auth Tracker
Check tracker daily for payer determination
Record auth number and valid date range in the order
Release order to scheduling
Schedule appointment within auth date range
Call patient with appointment confirmation and prep instructions

decisions.question: Is the patient's insurance coverage active?
branches: Yes: look up the CPT on the payer's auth-required list

No (inactive/termed): route to Financial Counseling for self-pay estimate; if patient accepts self-pay, mark self-pay and release to scheduling; if patient declines, FC cancels order and notifies provider

decisions.question: Does the payer require prior auth for this CPT code?
branches: No: call payer to confirm, document call ref # in order note, release to scheduling
Yes: gather clinical documentation

decisions.question: Is the clinical documentation sufficient (e.g., 6 weeks conservative treatment for spine)?
branches: Yes: submit through payer portal
No: message ordering provider for addendum and hold order up to 3 business days; if no response, escalate to clinic manager

decisions.question: What is the payer's determination?
branches: Approved: enter auth # and date range in order, release to scheduling
Needs more info: obtain info, resubmit under same ref #, resume daily checks (can repeat)
Denied: send denial letter to ordering provider for next steps

decisions.question: After a denial, does the provider want a peer-to-peer, and what is the outcome?
branches: P2P requested and denial overturned: treat as approval
P2P requested and denial upheld, or no P2P requested: provider chooses written appeal (packet prepared and given to Appeals team) or cancel order (call patient and close out)

edge_cases: Scan date moves past the auth end date: scheduling kicks it back; request an extension before the old auth expires, or submit a brand new auth if it already expired
URGENT/stat orders: scan proceeds without waiting for auth and a retro auth is submitted within 2 business days of the scan date

Provider doesn't respond to documentation request within 3 business days: escalate to clinic manager; payer 'needs more info' responses can loop multiple times; P2P must occur within 14 days of denial

trace_questions.question: What happens if a patient has active coverage, auth is required, the payer denies the request, the provider requests a peer-to-peer, and the denial is upheld?
trace_questions.answer: The provider chooses between a written appeal, in which case the auth staff put together the appeal packet and hand it to the Appeals team, or cancelling the order, in which case staff call the patient and close it out.

trace_questions.question: What happens if eligibility shows the patient's coverage is termed and the patient agrees to self-pay?
trace_questions.answer: No auth is started; the order goes to Financial Counseling for a self-pay estimate, FC sends it back after the patient agrees, and auth staff mark it self-pay and release it to scheduling with no auth needed.

title: Deceased Customer Notification and Account Settlement
workflow_text:
Notes for whoever covers estate desk while I'm out -- deceased customer accounts.

Usually starts w/ a family member calling or walking in. Get the date of death (DOD) and the relationship. Before ANY freeze we need a certified death cert (raised seal or state e-cert) plus gov ID from the person notifying us. If all they have is an obituary or it's a phone call only, just put a soft 'reported deceased' flag on the profile. No freeze, no closing anything until the certified copy shows up. People get this wrong constantly.

Once cert + ID are in hand: hard freeze on every account where the deceased is an owner. Cancel debit/credit cards, stop autopays and scheduled transfers. Do this same day.

After the freeze, pull the transaction history from DOD forward. Any Social Security / VA / other federal benefit deposits that landed after DOD have to go back to Treasury -- submit the reclamation and hold that amount. If there aren't any, skip ahead. Either way do this before you look at who gets the money.

Then ownership type:
- Joint w/ right of survivorship -> remove deceased from title, retitle to the survivor, lift the freeze for them. That's it, file ends there. Don't send joint accounts to legal.
- Sole owner -> check for a POD beneficiary on the account record.

POD on file: beneficiary brings their own ID + a copy of the death cert, branch ops supervisor signs off on the claim form. No estate docs, no legal review for POD.

No POD: depends on balance (after the reclamation hold).
  - Under $25,000 -> small estate affidavit, notarized.
  - $25,000 or more -> letters testamentary / letters of administration from probate court naming the executor.
Whichever one, send the package to Legal Review (internal queue, ~5 business days). If legal kicks it back, send the requester the rejection reasons and have them fix + resubmit -- goes back into legal again. BUT if legal rejects the same file a 2nd time, stop going back and forth, escalate to the Estate Services Manager, they take it from there.

heads up: if we asked the family for docs (affidavit, letters, corrected package, whatever) and hear nothing for 90 days, account stays frozen and you move the file to the Dormant Estate queue. Don't close it.

Payout once approved (supervisor sign-off for POD, or legal approval for estate): cashier's check payable to the beneficiary or to the estate (in the executor's name as rep, never personal). Then close the account(s) and mail the closure letter w/ the final interest statement.
stages: Receive death notification and record date of death and notifier relationship
Collect certified death certificate and notifier's government ID
Place hard freeze on all accounts where deceased is an owner
Cancel cards and stop autopays and scheduled transfers
Review deposits after date of death for federal benefits and submit reclamation to return them
Determine account ownership type
Retitle joint survivorship account to surviving owner and lift freeze
Check sole-owner account for a POD beneficiary
Obtain branch ops supervisor sign-off on POD beneficiary claim
Request small estate affidavit or letters testamentary/administration based on balance
Submit estate document package to Legal Review
Issue cashier's check to beneficiary or estate
Close account(s) and mail closure letter with final interest statement

decisions.question: Were any federal benefit deposits received after the date of death?
branches: Yes: submit reclamation to return them to Treasury and hold that amount, then continue
No: skip ahead to ownership review

decisions.question: Is the account joint with right of survivorship or sole-owner?
branches: Joint with survivorship: remove deceased, retitle to survivor, lift freeze; file ends (no legal review)
Sole owner: check for a POD beneficiary

decisions.question: Is a POD beneficiary on file for the sole-owner account?
branches: Yes: beneficiary provides ID and death cert copy, supervisor signs off, then cashier's check to beneficiary
No: go to estate document path based on balance

decisions.question: (No POD) Is the balance after any reclamation hold under $25,000?
branches: Under $25,000: require notarized small estate affidavit
$25,000 or more: require letters testamentary/administration from probate court

decisions.question: Does Legal Review approve the estate document package?
branches: Approved: issue cashier's check to the estate and close account
Rejected (first time): send reasons to requester, who corrects and resubmits to Legal Review (loop)
Rejected a second time: escalate to Estate Services Manager instead of sending back again

edge_cases: Notification by phone or obituary only without certified death certificate: place soft 'reported deceased' flag only; no freeze or closure until certified copy is received
Legal Review rejects the same file a second time: stop the resubmission loop and escalate to the Estate Services Manager
No response from the family for 90 days after requesting documents: account stays frozen and file moves to the Dormant Estate queue, not closed

trace_questions.question: What happens if a sole-owner account with no POD beneficiary has a $41,000 balance and Legal Review rejects the executor's documents twice?
trace_questions.answer: Because there is no POD and the balance is $25,000 or more, letters testamentary/administration are required and sent to Legal Review. After the first rejection the requester gets the reasons and resubmits; after the second rejection the file is escalated to the Estate Services Manager rather than being sent back again.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a sole-owner account with a POD beneficiary received a Social Security deposit after the date of death?
trace_questions.answer: After the freeze, the post-death Social Security deposit is returned to Treasury via reclamation and that amount is held. Then, since a POD beneficiary is on file, the beneficiary provides ID and a death cert copy, the branch ops supervisor signs off (no estate docs or legal review), a cashier's check is issued to the beneficiary, and the account is closed with a closure letter.

title: Outbound Parcel Pick, Pack, and Ship for Web Orders
workflow_text:
Hey - notes for covering the outbound parcel desk at the Riverside warehouse while I'm out.

Every morning around 7:30 pull the overnight web orders from the order queue in the WMS and release them as a pick wave. Print the pick lists (they come out sorted by aisle).

Pickers grab the items and scan each one at the bin. If the scanner says the bin is short (qty on hand < qty on the list):
- check the overflow rack in aisle 14 first
- if it's there, pick from overflow and carry on as normal
- if it's not in overflow either, mark the line "short" in the WMS and set the tote aside on the hold shelf. Customer Service gets an auto-alert and decides whether to ship partial or cancel. Don't pack anything off the hold shelf until CS updates the order.

Full totes go to the pack station. Packer rescans everything against the order so we catch wrong items, picks the box size, adds dunnage, and seals it.

Weigh the sealed box on the scale. If it's 10 lb or under it goes Ground Saver through Parcel Carrier A. Over 10 lb it goes standard Ground through Parcel Carrier B. The WMS prints the right label once you enter the weight - just double-check the carrier name on the label matches.

Slap the label on, then drop the box in the matching carrier cage (A cage by door 3, B cage by door 4).

Before the 3:00 pm pickup, scan out each cage to close the manifest so tracking numbers get emailed to customers.
stages: Pull overnight web orders from the WMS and release them as a pick wave
Print aisle-sorted pick lists
Pick items and scan each at the bin
Rescan items against the order at the pack station
Pack, add dunnage, and seal the box
Weigh the box and print the carrier label
Apply the label and place the box in the matching carrier cage
Scan out each cage to close the manifest before the 3:00 pm pickup

decisions.question: Is the bin short (quantity on hand less than quantity on the pick list)?
branches: No: pick normally and continue to the pack station
Yes: check the overflow rack in aisle 14; if the item is there, pick from overflow and continue as normal; if not, mark the line short in the WMS and place the tote on the hold shelf

decisions.question: Does the sealed box weigh 10 lb or less?
branches: Yes (10 lb or under): ship Ground Saver via Parcel Carrier A and place in the A cage by door 3
No (over 10 lb): ship standard Ground via Parcel Carrier B and place in the B cage by door 4

edge_cases: Item missing from both the bin and the overflow rack: the line is marked short, the tote goes to the hold shelf, Customer Service is auto-alerted to decide partial shipment or cancellation, and nothing is packed from the hold shelf until CS updates the order.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a picker finds the bin short, but the item is on the overflow rack in aisle 14, and the packed box weighs 12 lb?
trace_questions.answer: The picker picks from overflow and continues normally. At the pack station the items are rescanned, packed, and sealed. Because the box is over 10 lb, it ships standard Ground via Parcel Carrier B; it is labeled, placed in the B cage by door 4, and scanned out to close the manifest before the 3:00 pm pickup.

trace_questions.question: What happens if an item is short in its bin and is also not on the overflow rack?
trace_questions.answer: The picker marks the line short in the WMS and puts the tote on the hold shelf. Customer Service receives an auto-alert and decides whether to ship partial or cancel. The tote cannot be packed until CS updates the order.

title: Employment Verification Letter Requests
workflow_text:
Quick notes on handling employment verification requests (mortgage lenders, landlords, other employers, etc.). These come into the shared HR inbox at Northfield Services.

- First thing: log the request in the HR tracker with requester name, employee name, and date received.
- Check who sent it. If it came straight from the employee, we're fine to proceed. If it came from a third party (bank, landlord, etc.), it HAS to include a signed employee authorization form. No form = we don't release anything yet.
  - When the form is missing, email the employee and ask them to sign and return the authorization. Note the date you asked in the tracker.
  - If the employee sends it back, carry on as normal.
  - If we hear nothing after 5 business days, close the ticket and send the requester our standard "unable to verify without authorization" reply. Don't chase further; they can resubmit.
- Pull the employee up in the HRIS and confirm hire date, current job title, and employment status (active/terminated).
- Draft the letter from the Verification Letter template in the shared drive. Default letter only covers dates + title + status.
- If the request asks for salary/pay info, add it to the letter, but the HR manager has to sign off before it goes out. Send them the draft and wait for approval. No salary ask = no sign-off needed, just send.
- Send the letter to the requester (PDF, from the HR inbox).
- Save a copy in the employee's personnel file and close the ticket in the tracker.
stages: Log the request in the HR tracker
Confirm hire date, job title, and employment status in the HRIS
Draft the letter from the Verification Letter template
Get HR manager sign-off (only when salary info is included)
Send the letter to the requester as a PDF from the HR inbox
Save a copy in the personnel file and close the ticket

decisions.question: Did the request come from a third party without a signed employee authorization form?
branches: No (request from the employee, or third party with signed form): proceed to look up the employee in the HRIS
Yes: email the employee asking for a signed authorization and note the date in the tracker; proceed once it is returned

decisions.question: Does the request ask for salary/pay information?
branches: Yes: add salary to the letter and send the draft to the HR manager for sign-off before sending
No: send the standard letter (dates, title, status) without sign-off

edge_cases: If the employee does not return the signed authorization within 5 business days, close the ticket and send the requester the standard "unable to verify without authorization" reply; do not chase further, and the requester may resubmit.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a mortgage lender sends a request asking for salary but without an authorization form, and the employee returns the signed form two days later?
trace_questions.answer: HR logs the request and emails the employee for authorization. Once the form comes back, HR confirms details in the HRIS, drafts the letter including salary, sends it to the HR manager for sign-off, then after approval sends the PDF to the lender, saves a copy in the personnel file, and closes the ticket.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a landlord sends a request without an authorization form and the employee never responds?
trace_questions.answer: After 5 business days with no response, HR closes the ticket and sends the landlord the standard "unable to verify without authorization" reply. No letter is drafted and HR does not follow up further; the landlord can resubmit.

title: Family Practice Medical Records Release Requests
workflow_text:
Records release - how we handle it (for whoever's covering the records desk)

Requests come in by fax, through the patient portal, or dropped off at the front desk. First thing, log every request in the Release Tracker spreadsheet: patient name, DOB, who's asking, date received, and the date range of records they want.

Next, check the authorization form. It must be our standard release form (or an equivalent) and it needs ALL of the following:
- patient signature and date
- who the records are going to
- what records / date range

If anything is missing or unsigned, don't pull anything. Mail or fax the requester a blank form with a note circling what was missing, and set the tracker status to "On Hold - Auth." Check the hold list every Friday. If we still don't have a corrected form 30 days after we sent it back, change the status to "Closed - Incomplete" and send a short letter saying they'll need to submit a new request. Don't keep these open past 30 days.

Once the form is good, pull the records from the EHR for the requested date range only. Don't send the whole chart unless they asked for the whole chart.

Fees:
- Going provider-to-provider (another doctor's office, hospital, specialist) for continuity of care = no charge. Go straight to sending.
- Anyone else (patient wants own copy, attorney, insurance co., etc.) = send the invoice with the standard copy fee ($25 flat for electronic copies). Records do NOT go out until payment is received. Billing will email us when it's paid.

Sending: use the secure fax line or the encrypted email option in the EHR. Never regular email.

Last step: add a release note in the patient's chart (what was sent, to whom, date) and mark the tracker row "Completed."
stages: Log the request in the Release Tracker
Review the authorization form for completeness
Pull the requested records from the EHR for the specified date range
Send an invoice for the copy fee (non-provider requests only)
Send the records by secure fax or encrypted email
Add a release note to the patient's chart and mark the tracker entry Completed

decisions.question: Is the authorization form complete (patient signature and date, recipient, and records/date range)?
branches: Yes: proceed to pull the records from the EHR
No: send the requester a blank form noting what was missing and set tracker status to On Hold - Auth

decisions.question: Is the request provider-to-provider for continuity of care?
branches: Yes: no charge; send the records directly
No (patient, attorney, insurance company, etc.): send an invoice for the $25 copy fee and hold the records until Billing confirms payment

edge_cases: If a corrected authorization form is not received within 30 days of being sent back, the request is changed to Closed - Incomplete and the requester is sent a letter saying a new request must be submitted.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a patient submits a fully completed and signed form through the portal asking for a copy of their own records?
trace_questions.answer: The request is logged in the Release Tracker, the form passes the completeness check, and the records for the requested date range are pulled from the EHR. Because it is not a provider-to-provider request, the patient is invoiced the $25 copy fee, and the records are held until Billing emails that payment was received. The records are then sent by secure fax or encrypted email, a release note is added to the chart, and the tracker row is marked Completed.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a specialist's office faxes a request but the form is missing the patient's signature, and no corrected form comes back within 30 days?
trace_questions.answer: No records are pulled. The requester is sent a blank form with the missing signature noted, and the tracker status is set to On Hold - Auth. After 30 days with no corrected form, the status is changed to Closed - Incomplete and a letter is sent saying a new request must be submitted. The fact that it is a provider-to-provider request does not matter because the request never gets past the authorization check.

title: Stop Payment Request on a Personal Check
workflow_text:
Stop payments on personal checks - quick notes for new tellers / phone reps

These come in at the counter or by phone. Same steps either way. The only difference is the signature, explained below.

- First, verify the customer per standard ID procedure (photo ID at counter, security questions on phone). Only an account owner or authorized signer can place a stop.
- Get the check details: check #, exact amount, payee name, and the date written. Exact amount matters. The system matches on check # + amount, so push the customer to look at their register or app.
- Before entering anything, pull up account history and search for that check #.
  - If it has ALREADY CLEARED, we can't stop it. Tell the customer it's been paid. If they think it's fraud or a dispute with the payee, give them the Disputes team number. We're done at that point. No form and no fee.
  - If it hasn't cleared, keep going.
- Enter the stop payment order in CoreLink (Account Services > Stop Payment). Print the stop payment form and have the customer sign it.
- Fee: standard is $30, charged to the account the check is drawn on. If the customer is Premier tier (it shows on the profile banner), waive it. Use waiver code PRM in the fee screen. Everyone else gets charged the $30.
- Give the customer the confirmation # and let them know the stop is good for 6 months. After that they'd need to place a new one, which means a new fee unless Premier.
- Scan the signed form to the account file. Paper copy goes in the daily ops envelope.

Phone requests: obviously they can't sign in person. Enter the stop anyway and mark it ORAL in CoreLink. Then email or mail them the form. An oral stop only lasts 14 days. If the signed form isn't back by then, the system drops the stop automatically. Make sure you tell them this on the call. Once the form comes back, whoever receives it updates the stop from ORAL to WRITTEN, and the full 6 months then applies.
stages: Verify the customer's identity and authority on the account
Collect check details (check number, exact amount, payee, date)
Search account history for the check
Enter the stop payment order in CoreLink and obtain the customer's signature on the form
Charge or waive the stop payment fee
Give the customer the confirmation number and explain the 6-month validity
Scan the signed form to the account file and place the paper copy in the daily ops envelope

decisions.question: Has the check already cleared the account?
branches: Yes: the stop cannot be placed. Tell the customer it has been paid, refer them to the Disputes team if it is fraud or a payee dispute, and end the process with no form and no fee.
No: proceed to enter the stop payment order in CoreLink.

decisions.question: Is the customer Premier tier?
branches: Yes: waive the $30 fee using waiver code PRM.
No: charge the $30 fee to the account the check is drawn on.

edge_cases: Phone request: the customer cannot sign in person, so the stop is entered and marked ORAL, and the form is emailed or mailed. The oral stop lasts only 14 days and the system drops it automatically if the signed form is not returned. Once the form comes back, the stop is updated to WRITTEN and the full 6 months applies.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a non-Premier customer calls in to stop a check that has not cleared, and never returns the signed form?
trace_questions.answer: The rep verifies them with security questions, collects the check details, and confirms the check hasn't cleared. The rep then enters the stop in CoreLink marked ORAL, charges the $30 fee, and emails or mails the form. Because the signed form is not returned within 14 days, the system automatically drops the stop.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a Premier customer at the counter asks to stop a check that already cleared yesterday because they think it was fraudulent?
trace_questions.answer: After ID verification and collecting the check details, the account history shows the check has already cleared, so no stop can be placed. The customer is told it was paid and given the Disputes team number. No form is completed and no fee is charged. Premier status doesn't come into play because the process ends before the fee step.

title: Daily Cycle Count and Variance Resolution
workflow_text:
Cycle count notes for whoever is covering IC while I'm out. Ridgeway Logistics DC, Bldg 2.

Every morning before first wave:
