- Pull the day's count list from the WMS (Inventory > Cycle Count > Generate). It spits out ~40 bins weighted by ABC class. Print it or load it to your RF gun.
- Put a count hold on every bin on the list so pickers don't pull from them mid-count. Same screen, just select all > Hold.
- Count blind. The gun won't show you expected qty, that's on purpose. Key in what you physically see, eaches not cases.

Once you submit, the system compares your count to on-hand. Tolerance is under 2% AND under $50 ext. value. If it's inside tolerance the adjustment auto-posts and you're done with that bin. Pull the hold and move on.

Outside tolerance -> grab someone else (not you) to recount. Don't tell them your number.
  - Recount matches system qty: your first count was off. No adjustment, release hold, log it as "count error" in the variance tracker.
  - Recount matches your first count: variance is real, go research it.
  - Recount doesn't match either one: ask Dana (IC lead) to do a third count, then treat whatever Dana gets as the recount and go back through the same check.

Research = check for open picks not yet confirmed, putaways sitting unconfirmed, ASNs received but not put away, and the bins on either side (stuff gets slotted one over all the time).
  - If you find the cause, fix the transaction itself (confirm the putaway, confirm the pick, move qty from the neighbor bin, etc.). No adjustment needed. Release hold, log with the cause code.
  - If you can't explain it, key an adjustment request and send it to the shift supervisor for sign-off. They approve in the WMS, it posts, then you release the hold and log it as "unexplained."

Heads up: if a bin's been on hold more than 2 hrs and it's causing pick shortages on a wave, the supervisor can kill the hold early. If that happens, stop counting that bin and it goes back on tomorrow's list. Don't try to finish it mid-wave.

Tracker is the shared sheet, one row per bin that went out of tolerance.
stages: Generate the daily count list from the WMS
Place a count hold on all listed bins
Perform blind count and enter quantities
Have a different associate recount out-of-tolerance bins
Research the variance (open picks, unconfirmed putaways, unputaway ASNs, adjacent bins)
Correct the missed transaction or submit an adjustment request for supervisor sign-off
Post the approved adjustment
Release the count hold
Log the out-of-tolerance result in the variance tracker

decisions.question: Is the count variance within tolerance (under 2% and under $50 extended value)?
branches: Yes: adjustment auto-posts, release hold, move to next bin
No: have a different associate perform a blind recount

decisions.question: What does the recount match?
branches: Matches system qty: first count was an error; no adjustment, release hold, log as 'count error'
Matches first count: variance is real; research the cause
Matches neither: IC lead performs a third count, which is treated as the recount and re-evaluated

decisions.question: Can the variance cause be identified during research?
branches: Yes: fix the underlying transaction (confirm putaway/pick, move qty from neighbor bin); no adjustment; release hold and log with cause code
No: submit adjustment request to shift supervisor; after approval it posts, release hold, log as 'unexplained'

edge_cases: If the recount matches neither the first count nor the system, the IC lead does a third count and the process loops back through the recount check using that result.
If a bin has been on hold over 2 hours and is causing pick shortages on a wave, the supervisor can release the hold early; counting on that bin stops and it is re-queued to the next day's count list.

trace_questions.question: What happens if the first count is out of tolerance, the second associate's recount matches the first count, and research shows a putaway was never confirmed?
trace_questions.answer: The variance is treated as real, and research finds the cause. The associate confirms the putaway in the WMS instead of posting an adjustment, then releases the count hold and logs the bin in the variance tracker with the cause code.

trace_questions.question: What happens if the first count is out of tolerance, the recount matches neither the first count nor the system, and the IC lead's third count matches the first count but no cause can be found?
trace_questions.answer: The IC lead's count is treated as the recount. Because it matches the first count, the variance is real and gets researched. With no cause found, an adjustment request goes to the shift supervisor for sign-off. Once approved it posts, then the hold is released and the bin is logged as 'unexplained.'

title: Employee Referral Bonus Payout Processing
workflow_text:
Referral bonus notes, for whoever is covering the HR inbox while I'm out

Referrals come in through the referral form and land in the HR shared inbox. First thing, log it in the referral tracker (sheet in the HR drive): referrer name, candidate name, req #, date submitted.

Then look the candidate up in the ATS. If they already applied on their own within the last 6 months, the referral doesn't count. Send the referrer the "already in pipeline" template and close out the tracker row. Don't argue it, the policy is clear. If they're not in there, tag the candidate as a referral on their ATS profile so recruiting knows.

After that it's mostly waiting. Nothing gets paid at hire. When the ATS status flips to Hired, put a calendar reminder for start date + 90 days.

At 90 days:
- Ping the hiring manager to confirm the new hire is still with us and in good standing.
- Check HRIS that the referrer is still employed too. If the referrer has left the company, no payout. Close the row with the note "referrer separated."
- If the new hire left before hitting 90 days (this happens more than you'd think), there's no payout either. Send the referrer the "ineligible - separation" template and close the row. Sometimes you'll find out early from a term notice. Same handling, you don't have to wait for the reminder.

Amount: standard is $1,000. If the req is on the hard-to-fill list (also in the HR drive, updated quarterly) it's $2,500, and those need the department director's sign-off before payroll will process it. Standard amounts go straight to payroll.

Payroll cutoff is the 10th. Get the payout form in by then and it goes on the next cycle. Anything after the 10th rolls to the following cycle, so check the date before you tell anyone when they'll get paid.

Once submitted, email the referrer with the expected payout date and mark the tracker row Paid.
stages: Log the referral in the referral tracker
Look up the candidate in the ATS
Tag the candidate as a referral in the ATS
Set a 90-day reminder once the candidate is hired
Confirm with the hiring manager that the new hire is still employed and in good standing
Confirm in HRIS that the referrer is still employed
Determine the bonus amount using the hard-to-fill list
Obtain department director sign-off for hard-to-fill payouts
Submit the payout form to payroll
Email the referrer the expected payout date and mark the tracker row Paid

decisions.question: Did the candidate already apply on their own within the last 6 months?
branches: Yes: referral is ineligible; send the referrer the "already in pipeline" template and close the tracker row
No: tag the candidate as a referral in the ATS and continue

decisions.question: At 90 days, is the referrer still employed?
branches: No: no payout; close the tracker row with the note "referrer separated"
Yes: proceed to determine the bonus amount

decisions.question: Is the req on the hard-to-fill list?
branches: Yes: bonus is $2,500 and requires department director sign-off before submitting to payroll
No: bonus is the standard $1,000 and goes straight to payroll

edge_cases: The new hire separates before reaching 90 days: no payout; send the referrer the "ineligible - separation" template and close the row, which can be done as soon as a term notice arrives without waiting for the 90-day reminder.
The payout form is submitted after the 10th: it misses the payroll cutoff and rolls to the following pay cycle instead of the next one, which changes the payout date given to the referrer.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a referred candidate who was not already in the ATS is hired into a hard-to-fill req, both the new hire and the referrer are still employed at 90 days, and the director's sign-off comes back on the 14th of the month?
trace_questions.answer: The bonus is $2,500. Because it needs director sign-off, it can't go to payroll until the 14th. That is after the 10th cutoff, so it rolls to the following pay cycle instead of the next one. The referrer is emailed with that later payout date, and the tracker row is marked Paid.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a referral is logged and tagged, the candidate is hired, but by the 90-day check the hiring manager confirms the new hire is in good standing while HRIS shows the referrer has left the company?
trace_questions.answer: No bonus is paid. The tracker row is closed with the note "referrer separated," and nothing is sent to payroll.

title: Outpatient Lab Critical Result Callback
workflow_text:
Critical value callbacks: how we handle them on the triage line

When the lab system fires a critical alert (red flag in the results inbox), it comes to whoever is on triage. Note the time you picked it up in the critical log right away. The 60-min clock starts from the lab's flag time, not when you open it.

First, match the result to the patient using name + DOB. If either doesn't match what's in our chart, stop and call the lab back to sort it out before doing anything else. Don't page a provider on an unconfirmed result.

Once it's confirmed:
- Page the ordering provider (pager # is on the order).
- Give them 15 min to call back. No callback means page again.
- Still nothing 15 min after the 2nd page? Go to the on-call provider for that day (on-call sheet at the front desk). If on-call is also unreachable, call the medical director's cell. Log every page attempt with the time.

When a provider calls back, read the value back to them word for word and have them confirm. Document provider name, time, and "read back confirmed" in the result note.

Provider tells you what to do with the patient. Usually one of two things:
* Go to the ED now. Call the patient, tell them to go to the nearest ED, and call the ED charge nurse at Riverside General with a quick handoff (name, DOB, the value, who ordered it).
* Not urgent enough for ED (med hold, repeat lab tomorrow, etc). Call the patient and give the exact instructions. If it's a repeat lab, put the order in and tell them our draw hours.

Calling the patient: try the primary number, then the alternate. If no answer, leave a callback msg (no results on voicemail, just "call the clinic re: your lab work") and try again. 3 attempts total, spread over about an hour. If you still haven't reached them after the 3rd, let the provider know. The provider decides whether to request a police welfare check or send a letter. Don't close the alert in that case. Mark it "open, pt not reached" in the log and hand it off verbally to the next triage nurse.

Once the patient is reached and has the instructions, document the call in the chart (what you told them, that they understood). Then close the alert in the critical log with the close time.
stages: Pick up critical lab alert and log time received
Verify result matches patient using name and DOB
Page ordering provider
Read back critical value to responding provider and document confirmation
Receive provider's instructions for patient
Call patient (primary, then alternate number) and give instructions
Call ED charge nurse with handoff (if ED referral) or enter repeat lab order (if repeat lab)
Document patient call in chart
Close alert in critical log with close time

decisions.question: Do the patient name and DOB on the result match the chart?
branches: Yes: proceed to page the ordering provider
No: stop and call the lab back to resolve before paging anyone

decisions.question: Does the ordering provider call back within 15 minutes?
branches: Yes: read back the value and get instructions
No: page again; if no callback 15 min after the 2nd page, contact the on-call provider, then the medical director's cell if on-call is unreachable

decisions.question: Does the provider direct the patient to the ED?
branches: Yes: tell patient to go to the nearest ED and call the Riverside General ED charge nurse with a handoff
No: give the patient the provider's specific instructions (e.g., med hold, repeat lab); if repeat lab, enter the order and give draw hours

decisions.question: Is the patient reached within 3 call attempts?
branches: Yes: give instructions, document the call, close the alert
No: notify provider (who decides on welfare check or letter), mark alert 'open, pt not reached,' and verbally hand off to next triage nurse

edge_cases: Ordering provider does not respond: repeat page after 15 min, then escalate to on-call provider, then medical director, logging every attempt with time
Patient unreachable after 3 attempts over about an hour: alert stays open, provider decides on welfare check or letter, verbal handoff to next shift
Name or DOB mismatch on the result: no provider is paged until the lab resolves the discrepancy

trace_questions.question: What happens if the ordering provider does not answer either page, the on-call provider calls back and says the patient needs the ED, and the patient answers on the first call?
trace_questions.answer: After 15 min with no response to the 2nd page, the nurse contacts the on-call provider and reads back the value with confirmation documented. The nurse tells the patient to go to the nearest ED, calls the Riverside General ED charge nurse with a handoff (name, DOB, value, ordering provider), documents the patient call in the chart, and closes the alert in the critical log with the close time.

trace_questions.question: What happens if the provider orders a repeat lab for tomorrow but the patient cannot be reached after three call attempts?
trace_questions.answer: The nurse enters the repeat lab order, then lets the provider know the patient was not reached. The provider decides whether to request a police welfare check or send a letter. The alert is not closed. It is marked 'open, pt not reached' in the log and verbally handed off to the next triage nurse.

title: Cashier's Check Issuance at Teller Window
workflow_text:
Cashier's checks – teller window notes (for new hires covering the line)

Customer has to be an account holder at Riverbend Community Bank. Non-customers go to the service desk, we don't sell official checks to walk-ins.

- Get ID, match it to the profile, and make sure they're an owner on the account the money is coming from. Authorized signers on a business acct are OK, check the signer card.
- Get the payee name EXACTLY as they want it printed. Spell it back to them. Get the amount and the remitter name (defaults to the account holder; don't let them put someone else's name as remitter).
- Look at AVAILABLE balance, not ledger. Holds don't count. Available has to cover the check amount plus the $10 fee.
  - Not enough? Ask if they have another acct with us they want to move money from. If yes, do the internal transfer and recheck. If no, tell them we can't issue it for that amount. Either they pick a lower amount (start the balance check over) or we're done. Don't override, ever.
- Fee: $10. Premier Checking and Premier Savings get it waived, the system usually flags it but double-check the product code because it doesn't always.
- Anything over $10,000 needs a supervisor override in OCS before it will let you print. Call your sup over, they key their ID in. Under $10k you just proceed.
- Debit the acct (amount + fee if applicable), then print on the official check stock in the locked drawer.
- Hold the printed check up and have the customer look at payee + amount before you sign. You sign. Over $10k the supervisor countersigns too.
- Customer gets the check and the customer copy/receipt. Bank copy goes in the official check batch envelope for end of day.

Printer jams / prints wrong / customer spots a typo AFTER printing: do NOT hand it over. Write VOID across the face, enter serial # on the void log, put the voided check in the batch envelope, and reprint (new serial). No second fee. If the error was over $10k the sup has to re-approve the reprint.
stages: Verify customer ID and confirm ownership or signer authority on the funding account
Confirm payee name, amount, and remitter with the customer
Check available balance against amount plus fee
Determine whether the $10 fee applies
Obtain supervisor override in OCS if required
Debit the account for the check amount and any fee
Print the cashier's check on official check stock
Have the customer review payee and amount on the printed check
Sign the check (with supervisor countersignature if required)
Give the customer the check and receipt and file the bank copy in the official check batch

decisions.question: Does the available balance cover the check amount plus the fee?
branches: Yes: continue to fee determination and processing
No, and customer has another account with funds: do an internal transfer and recheck the balance
No, and no other funds: customer may choose a lower amount (recheck balance) or the request is declined; no overrides

decisions.question: Is the funding account a Premier Checking or Premier Savings product?
branches: Yes: waive the $10 fee
No: charge the $10 fee

decisions.question: Is the check amount over $10,000?
branches: Yes: supervisor must enter an override in OCS before printing and must countersign the check
No: teller proceeds to print and signs alone

edge_cases: Insufficient available balance loops back: after an internal transfer or a reduced amount, the balance check is repeated; holds never count toward available balance and the teller may never override

Printer jam, misprint, or a typo caught after printing: write VOID on the check, record the serial on the void log, place it in the batch envelope, and reprint with a new serial at no extra fee; checks over $10,000 need supervisor re-approval for the reprint

trace_questions.question: What happens if a Premier Checking customer with sufficient available funds requests a $12,500 cashier's check?
trace_questions.answer: The $10 fee is waived because it is a Premier account. Because the amount is over $10,000, a supervisor must key an override into OCS before the check can print. The account is debited $12,500, the check is printed, the customer reviews it, the teller signs and the supervisor countersigns, then the customer gets the check and receipt and the bank copy goes in the batch envelope.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a standard (non-Premier) checking customer requests a $4,000 check but available balance is only $3,500, and they have $6,000 in a savings account with the bank?
trace_questions.answer: The teller offers an internal transfer from savings, completes it, and rechecks the available balance, which must cover $4,010 ($4,000 plus the $10 fee since the account is not Premier). Once it does, no supervisor override is needed because the amount is under $10,000; the account is debited $4,010, the check is printed, reviewed by the customer, signed by the teller alone, and handed over with the receipt.

title: Internal Transfer Request Processing
workflow_text:
Internal transfers - notes for whoever covers the HR inbox while I'm out

Requests come in through the transfer form and land in the HR inbox. Open a ticket for each one right away; everything gets logged there.

First thing, check eligibility in the HRIS:
- Must be 12+ months in the current role.
- No active PIP. If there's an active PIP, decline it outright with the standard decline email. No exceptions, and don't ask the manager.
- Under 12 months: email the current manager and ask if they'll waive the tenure rule. If they waive it, carry on as normal. If they won't, decline and close the ticket.

Once eligibility is OK, send the current manager the release sign-off form. They can't actually block a transfer. They either release on the normal timeline or ask for a delayed release, which we cap at 60 days. If they ask for a delay, note it on the ticket. It only matters when we set the effective date later. If they haven't answered in 5 business days, escalate to their skip-level manager. Don't just sit on it.

After the release form is back, forward the packet to the hiring manager so they can schedule the interview. We don't run these interviews. Just chase them for an outcome afterward.
- Not selected: send the employee the not-selected note (cc the current manager) and close.
- Selected: request a comp review from the comp team.

Comp review: if the proposed pay is within 10% of current pay, it's a standard offer and you can go straight to the offer letter. If it's an increase over 10%, the HR director has to approve. If the director rejects it, it goes back to comp to revise and then through the same 10% check again. This can bounce a couple of times. That's normal.

Then prep the offer letter and send it to the employee.
- Accepts: set the effective date with both managers. Respect any delayed release from earlier (max 60 days out).
- Declines: notify both managers and close.
- Counters: back to comp review, and the same 10%/director rule applies. They only get ONE counter. A second counter is treated as a decline, so notify both managers and close.

After the date is set, update the HRIS record (title, dept, manager, pay). Then notify payroll and IT. Btw, if the new role is in a different state, flag it to payroll specifically so they set up new tax withholding before the effective date.

Last step: close the ticket and file the signed offer + release form in the employee file.

title: Outbound Truckload Carrier Tendering and Spot Booking
workflow_text:
Load tendering - notes for covering my desk next week

Load requests drop into the Outbound Loads shared queue from the order desk, usually by 10am. Pull each one and check pallet count, total weight, and ship date against the sales order. The order desk gets these wrong a lot, so don't trust the summary line.

First thing: is it even a truckload? 12+ pallets OR 15,000 lb or more = FTL, go through the routing guide. Anything under both = LTL. Don't tender LTL in the TMS. Just book it in the LTL rate portal (cheapest approved carrier it shows is fine) and skip straight to the dock appointment step below.

FTL:
- look up the lane (origin DC > dest zip3) in the routing guide. Carriers are ranked: primary, then backups.
- tender in TMS to the top carrier you haven't tried yet.
- they get 2 hrs to accept. No response in 2 hrs = treat it as a reject. Don't sit around waiting, just move on.
- rejected? tender to the next carrier down the list. Keep going down the guide until someone accepts.
- if you run out of carriers in the guide -> spot market. Email at least 3 brokers from the approved broker list for quotes.

Spot quotes: take the lowest one. If it's within 15% of the contract rate for that lane (rate is in the routing guide), you can just award it yourself. Over 15% needs the logistics manager to OK it first. If the manager approves, award it. If they say no, they usually want the ship date pushed. Send it back to the order desk to renegotiate the date with the customer, and it'll come back through the queue as a new request. Note: manager isn't around after 4pm. Anything over-threshold after that goes to the on-call transportation director instead. Don't hold it overnight.

Once a carrier is locked in (guide, spot, or LTL), book the pickup appointment with the dock scheduler. Then send the BOL + load details to the carrier, and update the sales order with carrier name and PRO #. The customer service team pulls tracking off that, so don't skip it.

Day of pickup, watch the dock board. If the driver hasn't shown 2+ hrs after the appointment, call it a bounce. Mark the bounce on that carrier's scorecard, then re-tender starting with the next carrier in the guide after the one that bounced (or spot if none left), and rebook the dock appt. Same deal if a carrier accepts and then cancels on you before pickup: treat it like a reject and move to the next carrier.

After pickup actually happens, log the tender results (accepts/rejects/timeouts per carrier) in the carrier scorecard sheet. Procurement uses it for the quarterly bid.

title: Post-Discharge Follow-Up Phone Calls (Primary Care Transitions Team)
workflow_text:
TCM call notes - for whoever is covering my queue next week

Goal: every patient discharged from Lakeside Regional to one of our PCPs gets a call within 2 business days. Here's how I run it.

Mornings: pull the discharge list from the hospital feed (the Transitions report, not the ADT screen, the ADT screen misses obs stays). Split it between whoever's on calls that day, about even, and put each name in the shared TCM queue under your initials.

BEFORE you dial anyone, read the discharge summary. You need the diagnosis, the new med list, and any follow-up the hospital already ordered. Don't skip this, it's how you catch the med problems later.

If the patient shows as inpatient again when you open the chart (readmitted), don't call. Close the task as "readmitted" and you're done. The new discharge will come back through the feed.

Calling:
- Verify with 2 identifiers (name + DOB). If someone else answers, check the authorized contacts in the chart. If they're listed, go ahead with them. If not, just ask for a callback at our number. Don't discuss anything. That counts as a no-contact attempt.
- No answer -> leave a generic VM (no diagnosis info), log it as attempt #1, and retry next business day. Max 3 attempts. After the 3rd miss, mail the outreach letter and send a staff message to the PCP so they know we never reached them. Then close.
- Wrong number / disconnected = don't bother with more attempts. Go straight to the letter + PCP message, and also send a ticket to registration to fix the phone number.

Once you've got them: symptom screen first (script is in the shared drive). If anything on the red flag list comes up you have to figure out how bad. Chest pain, trouble breathing, confusion, fainting -> tell them to hang up and call 911, end the call, and message the PCP right away marked urgent. Anything else on the red flag list (fever over 101, wound redness, swelling, etc.) -> warm transfer to the triage nurse line while they're still on the phone. After the triage handoff you still come back and finish the med rec and appointment piece with them later that day; for the 911 people you don't, just document.

Med rec: go through what they're actually taking vs. the discharge list. If anything doesn't match (missing new med, still taking something that was stopped, dose confusion) send a pharmacist review message, they get back within 24h. Keep going with the call, don't wait on pharmacy.

Appointment: they need a PCP visit within 7 days of discharge. If one's already on the books in that window, just confirm it with them. If not, schedule it. If the PCP has nothing within 7 days, book with the NP on that care team instead.

Last: document the call in the TCM note template (attempts, screen results, med rec, appt) and close the task in the queue.

Assign patients to call staff in the shared TCM queue
Review the discharge summary (diagnosis, new meds, ordered follow-up)
Call the patient and verify identity with two identifiers
Run the symptom screening script
Perform medication reconciliation against the discharge list
Confirm or schedule a follow-up visit within 7 days of discharge
Document the call in the TCM note template
Close the task in the queue

branches: Yes: do not call; close the task as 'readmitted'
No: proceed with the call

Unauthorized person answers: ask only for a callback; counts as a no-contact attempt
No answer: leave a generic voicemail, log the attempt, retry next business day; after the 3rd failed attempt, mail the outreach letter, message the PCP, and close
Wrong or disconnected number: skip further attempts, mail the letter, message the PCP, and send a registration ticket to fix the number

branches: No red flags: continue to medication reconciliation
Severe red flag (chest pain, trouble breathing, confusion, fainting): instruct patient to call 911, end the call, send urgent message to PCP, document only (no med rec/appointment)
Other red flag (e.g., fever over 101, wound redness, swelling): warm transfer to triage nurse line, then return later that day to finish med rec and appointment

branches: Yes: continue to appointment step
No: send pharmacist review message (response within 24h) and continue the call without waiting

branches: Yes: confirm it with the patient
No: schedule with the PCP; if the PCP has no availability within 7 days, book with the care team NP

Someone other than the patient answers and is not an authorized contact: no information is discussed, only a callback request, and it counts as a failed attempt toward the 3-attempt limit

trace_questions.answer: The spouse is only asked for a callback and nothing is discussed; this counts as attempt #1. The next two calls get generic voicemails and are logged as attempts #2 and #3. After the third miss, the outreach letter is mailed, a staff message is sent to the PCP saying the patient was never reached, and the task is closed.

trace_questions.answer: Fever over 101 is a non-severe red flag, so the patient is warm-transferred to the triage nurse line. Later that day the caller returns to finish: the medication mismatch triggers a pharmacist review message (reply within 24h) while the call continues, and since the PCP has nothing within 7 days, the visit is booked with the care team NP. The call is then documented in the TCM template and the task closed.

title: Mobile Deposit Exception Queue Review
workflow_text:
Mobile deposit exceptions - how I work the queue (for whoever covers me next week)

Queue lives in DepositReview > Exceptions. Grab the oldest item first, always. Hard cutoff is 6pm ET. Anything not dispositioned by 6 rolls to the next business day and the deposit date moves with it, so the customer's funds are effectively a day later. If something has been sitting unworked for more than 2 business days, the supervisor gets an auto-alert, so please don't let that happen.

Last thing on every item, accept or reject: log the disposition plus the reason code in the queue tracker. People forget this step and then we can't count re-submits. More on that below.

Before anything else, look at the check date. If it's more than 6 months old (stale), reject it as R4 and stop there. EXCEPTION: US Treasury checks are good for 1 year, so don't kill those at 6 months.

Then look at the images.
- Front and back both have to be legible: MICR line, amounts, payee.
- The back must carry the endorsement "For mobile deposit only at Riverside Community Bank" plus a signature.
If either is bad, reject R1. The customer gets the standard email telling them to retake the photos and resubmit. Resubmits drop right back into this queue as new items, so you'll see the same check again and run it through everything from the top. On the 3rd R1 rejection for the same check (that's why we log!), use the R1-B template instead. It tells them to bring the check to a branch, and you put a block on that check number in mobile so they can't keep retrying.

Amounts: compare the written (legal) amount to what the customer keyed in.
- They match → move on.
- They don't match and the difference is $25 or less → correct the item to the WRITTEN amount, add a note, and keep going.
- The difference is more than $25 → reject R2 and have the customer resubmit with the correct amount. Don't try to fix it yourself.

After the images and amounts, run the duplicate search (Tools > Dup Presentment). If it hits, meaning the same check was already deposited with us, reject R3. Also look at the account's history: if this account had ANOTHER duplicate hit within the last 90 days, fill out the referral form to Fraud Ops. When you refer to Fraud, DO NOT send the customer the R3 email. Fraud handles the contact. You still log it in the tracker.

If it clears all of that, figure out the hold.
- Account opened less than 30 days ago, OR the item is over $5,000 → extended hold, 7 business days.
- Otherwise → standard hold: $225 available next business day, the rest on the second business day.
Apply the hold in the system, then accept the item so it releases to posting. Then send the acceptance email. That email already has the hold dates merged in, so check they look right before sending.

Rejections all get the matching reason-code email (R1/R1-B/R2/R3/R4), except the Fraud case above.

Check the check date for staleness
Review front and back images for legibility and the required endorsement
Compare the written amount to the customer-keyed amount
Run the duplicate presentment search
Determine the hold type based on account age and item amount
Apply the hold in the system
Accept the item and release it to posting
Send the customer the acceptance or reason-code rejection email
Log the disposition and reason code in the queue tracker

Yes → send the R1-B email directing the customer to bring the check to a branch, and block that check number in mobile

The duplicate search and hold step are never reached, so the new-account extended hold does not apply on this pass.

title: Triage of a Reported Phishing Email
workflow_text:
Phish inbox coverage - notes for whoever has the rotation this week

When someone forwards a suspicious email to the phish-report mailbox at Harborview Supply Co., here's the drill:

- Open a ticket in the security tracker within 1 hr of the report. Put in the sender address, subject line, and who reported it.
- Grab the full headers from the original message (not the forward). Submit any links/attachments to the sandbox.

Once the sandbox finishes, make the call:
* Sandbox clean AND headers check out (SPF/DKIM pass, sender is a known vendor/partner) -> it's a false positive. Reply to the reporter thanking them, note "FP" in the ticket, close it. Done, skip everything below.
* Anything else (sandbox flags it, or headers look spoofed) -> treat as malicious and keep going.

Heads up: the sandbox sometimes hangs. If you don't have a verdict after 30 min, don't wait on it. Treat the email as malicious and continue with the steps below.

Malicious path:
- Search the mail logs for every other recipient of the same message.
- Purge it from all mailboxes using the admin console.
- Check the web proxy logs to see if anyone clicked the link / opened the attachment.
   - If someone did: reset that user's password, isolate their laptop from the endpoint console, and page the IT on-call so they can follow up.
   - If nobody did: nothing extra, move on.
- Send the reporter a short note that it was confirmed malicious and removed, add your notes to the ticket, close it.
stages: Open a ticket in the security tracker with sender, subject, and reporter
Pull the original headers and submit links/attachments to the sandbox
Search the mail logs for other recipients of the message
Purge the message from all mailboxes
Check the web proxy logs for clicks or opened attachments
Notify the reporter, add notes to the ticket, and close it

decisions.question: Is the sandbox result clean and do the headers check out (SPF/DKIM pass, known sender)?
branches: Yes: mark as false positive, thank the reporter, note FP in the ticket, and close it with no further steps
No (sandbox flags it or headers look spoofed): treat as malicious and continue to search mail logs and purge

decisions.question: Did any user click the link or open the attachment according to the proxy logs?
branches: Yes: reset that user's password, isolate their laptop from the endpoint console, and page the IT on-call, then notify the reporter and close the ticket
No: take no extra action and proceed to notify the reporter and close the ticket

edge_cases: If the sandbox returns no verdict within 30 minutes, the email is treated as malicious without waiting and the malicious path (search logs, purge, check proxy) continues.

trace_questions.question: What happens if the sandbox hangs with no verdict after 30 minutes and the proxy logs show one employee clicked the link?
trace_questions.answer: The email is treated as malicious. The analyst searches the mail logs for other recipients, purges the message from all mailboxes, then because a user clicked, resets that user's password, isolates their laptop from the endpoint console, and pages the IT on-call. Finally the reporter is told it was confirmed malicious and removed, and the ticket is noted and closed.

trace_questions.question: What happens if the sandbox comes back clean and the headers pass SPF/DKIM from a known vendor?
trace_questions.answer: It is a false positive. The analyst replies to the reporter to thank them, notes FP in the ticket, and closes it. No mail log search, purge, or proxy check is done.

title: Graduate Thesis Format Review and Final Deposit
workflow_text:
Thesis office – format review notes (for Dana while I'm out)

Students upload the final PDF + the signed approval page through the Graduate School portal. The queue sorts by upload date, so work oldest first.

First thing: open the approval page. Every committee member listed on the student's record needs a signature (wet or digital, both ok). If anyone's missing, put the submission on HOLD and email the student with the missing name(s). Don't start the format check until the page is complete. The clock doesn't run for us while it's on hold.

Once signatures are good:
- Go through the format checklist (margins, page numbering, TOC matches headings, figure/table captions, references style consistent)
- Mark up the PDF with comments for anything off

If you find problems, send the marked-up PDF back with the standard corrections email. They fix and re-upload, and it goes back into your queue. Re-check the whole thing, not just the flagged items, because people break other stuff while fixing.
** If it's the 3rd round of corrections, don't just send it back again. Book them a 30-min appointment with Priya (senior reviewer) before they re-upload.

Clean PDF → check the embargo box on the submission form.
- No embargo: go straight to approval.
- Embargo requested: forward the form + justification to the Assoc. Dean's office. If they approve, set the 2-yr embargo flag before approving. If they deny, email the student that it'll publish normally, then continue as usual.

Approval = change status to "Format Approved" in the system. That pushes the file to the library repository automatically, but double check it shows up in the repository staging list the next day.

title: Intern Hiring Pipeline at Northgate Logistics Group
workflow_text:
Intern hiring - how I run it (for whoever covers while I'm out)

Posting closes on the date in the req. Next morning, export all apps from the careers portal into the tracker sheet (one row per applicant).

First pass is just eligibility, no judgment calls:
- must be currently enrolled (degree program, not just a cert course)
- expected grad date has to be AFTER the internship end date
If either fails -> send 'Not Eligible' template from the shared inbox, mark row grey, done. Everyone else goes to the hiring manager as a batch with resumes attached.

Mgr flags who they want to talk to. They usually reply in a day or two. If nothing back after 3 business days, cc the dept head on a nudge. Don't wait longer than that, the good candidates get snapped up.

For the flagged ones: book a 20-min phone screen (use the scheduling link, not back-and-forth emails). Recruiter does the screen and scores 1-5 on the rubric.
- 3 or higher -> panel interview
- exactly 2 -> 'hold' tab. don't reject yet, these are our backups
- 1 -> 'Not Selected' template

Panel = mgr + one team member, 45 min. Get both feedback forms in before anything moves. Once the mgr names their pick, put in the offer approval request to HR budget (stipend amount + dates). Offer letter goes out only after budget signs off.

Candidate has 5 business days to respond.
- accepts -> log it in tracker, send the onboarding team the name/start date/mgr, close the req once all slots filled
- declines -> go back to the panel'd candidates first; if none left the mgr wants, pull the top person from the hold tab and run them through panel
- no response by day 5 -> one follow-up call + email, give 2 more business days. Still nothing = treat as a decline.

Screen applicants for eligibility (enrollment and graduation date)
Send eligible applicants' resumes to the hiring manager
Hiring manager selects candidates to advance
Schedule phone screens via the scheduling link
Conduct and score phone screens on the 1-5 rubric
Hold panel interviews (manager + team member) and collect both feedback forms
Hiring manager selects a finalist
Submit offer approval request to HR budget
Send offer letter after budget approval
Log acceptance and hand off to the onboarding team

branches: Yes: included in the batch sent to the hiring manager
No: sent the 'Not Eligible' template, row marked grey, process ends for them

branches: 3 or higher: advance to panel interview

1: sent the 'Not Selected' template

Declines: offer goes to another panel-interviewed candidate the manager wants; if none, top hold-tab candidate is run through a panel interview

trace_questions.answer: After 5 business days, the recruiter makes one follow-up call and email and allows 2 more business days; with still no response it is treated as a decline, so the offer moves to another panel-interviewed candidate the manager wants or, if none, the top hold-tab candidate goes to a panel interview.

title: Laptop Hardware Failure and Loaner Swap
workflow_text:
Laptop hardware failures - how we handle them (for new desk staff)

When someone calls/emails saying their laptop is dead, won't boot, screen cracked, keyboard dying, etc., log it in the queue under Hardware > Laptop. Grab the asset tag off the bottom sticker (ask the user to read it if remote). No asset tag = can't do anything downstream, so don't skip it.

First thing, try remote diagnostics if the machine powers on at all - run the vendor health check tool through the remote session. A lot of "broken" laptops are driver or battery-calibration issues. If you can fix it remotely, fix it, note what you did, and close the ticket. Done.

If it's actual hardware:
- Look up the asset tag in the asset register to check warranty end date.
- Under warranty -> open an RMA on the vendor portal. Vendor handles parts + labor, no cost to us.
- Out of warranty -> get a repair quote from the local repair shop we use, and send the quote to the user's manager. Manager has to approve because it gets charged to their dept.
  - Approved -> device goes to the repair shop.
  - Declined -> device gets retired. Mark it retired in the asset register and open a new-device request ticket for the user; that follows the procurement process, not this one, so close this ticket with a link to the new one.

Either way (RMA or approved shop repair), the user needs a loaner before their laptop leaves the building. Pull one from the loaner cabinet, sign it out on the loaner sheet with the user's name + date.

IMPORTANT - user's data has to come off the drive before it goes out. Copy their profile folders to the user's home share. Vendors sometimes swap the drive and we never get it back.

Then pack and ship (RMA) or drop off (repair shop). Put the tracking/drop-off ref in the ticket.

When it comes back: reimage it with the standard build, restore the user's data from the home share, then book a time to swap it with them and collect the loaner. Check the loaner back in on the sheet. Close ticket.

Odd stuff:
- Loaner cabinet empty: don't hold up the repair. Put the user on the loaner waitlist (pinned in the team channel) and tell them to use a hot-desk PC in the meantime. First loaner returned goes to whoever's top of the list.
- Vendor RMA not back in 10 business days: escalate to our vendor account rep. If still nothing, the user keeps the loaner permanently - reassign it to them in the asset register and pull a new loaner from stock to refill the cabinet.
stages: Log the ticket under Hardware > Laptop with the asset tag
Run remote diagnostics via the vendor health check tool
Check warranty status in the asset register
Open a vendor RMA or obtain a repair shop quote and send it to the manager
Issue a loaner laptop and sign it out on the loaner sheet
Back up the user's profile folders to their home share
Ship the device to the vendor or drop it off at the repair shop and record the reference
Reimage the returned device and restore the user's data
Swap the device back with the user and check the loaner back in
Close the ticket

decisions.question: Can the issue be fixed through remote diagnostics?
branches: Yes: fix it remotely, document the fix, and close the ticket
No (actual hardware fault): proceed to warranty check

decisions.question: Is the laptop still under warranty?
branches: Yes: open an RMA on the vendor portal at no cost
No: get a repair quote from the local repair shop and send it to the user's manager for approval

decisions.question: Does the manager approve the out-of-warranty repair quote?
branches: Approved: device goes to the repair shop (after loaner issued and data backed up)
Declined: mark the device retired in the asset register, open a new-device request ticket for procurement, and close this ticket with a link to it

edge_cases: Loaner cabinet is empty: the repair proceeds anyway; the user is added to the loaner waitlist pinned in the team channel, uses a hot-desk PC meanwhile, and gets the first loaner returned if top of the list

Vendor RMA not returned within 10 business days: escalate to the vendor account rep; if still unresolved, the loaner is permanently reassigned to the user in the asset register and a new loaner is pulled from stock to refill the cabinet

trace_questions.question: What happens if a laptop has a genuine hardware fault, is out of warranty, and the user's manager declines the repair quote?
trace_questions.answer: The device is not repaired. It is marked retired in the asset register, a new-device request ticket is opened for the user (handled by procurement), and the original ticket is closed with a link to the new one. No loaner swap or shipping happens under this process.

trace_questions.question: What happens if an in-warranty laptop is sent out on RMA and the vendor still hasn't returned it after 10 business days and escalation to the account rep?
trace_questions.answer: The user keeps the loaner permanently: it is reassigned to them in the asset register, and a new loaner is pulled from stock to refill the loaner cabinet.

title: Handling a Lost or Stolen Company Laptop Report
workflow_text:
Lost/stolen laptop reports - notes for whoever is covering the security desk

These come in by phone or the service portal. First thing: open a ticket under DEVICE-LOSS and get the user's story down (when and where they last had it, and whether they think it was lost or taken). Don't skip the 'lost vs stolen' question. It matters later.

Once you've pulled the asset record (search by user if they don't know the serial), check the encryption field. Before you touch the device, kill the account side:
- force a password reset on the user's account
- revoke all active sessions + refresh tokens (email, VPN, SSO)
- tell the user how to get back in from a loaner or their phone

Then the device itself:
- Encryption shows ENCRYPTED with key escrowed -> send a remote LOCK from the MDM console. Standard path.
- Encryption shows anything else (NOT ENCRYPTED, UNKNOWN, or encrypted but key not escrowed) -> treat it as unencrypted. Skip the lock and send a remote WIPE right away. Also email the Privacy Office with the ticket # so they can start a possible-data-exposure review. Note in the ticket that you notified them.

On the standard path, watch the MDM console for the device to check in and confirm the lock. If it hasn't checked in within 24 hrs of the lock command, queue a wipe anyway and note it. We don't wait longer than that.

Stolen vs lost:
- Stolen -> user has to file a police report and give us the report number. Put the ticket on hold until we have it. No replacement gets ordered without it (insurance requirement).
- Lost -> no police report needed. Go ahead.
- If a stolen-device user hasn't sent the report # after 5 business days, cc their manager on a reminder. Keep the ticket on hold.

After that, submit the replacement request to IT procurement and link it to the ticket. Last step: mark the asset LOST or STOLEN in inventory (whichever matches) and close the ticket.

If the device turns up after we've started: the user does NOT just log back in on it. They bring it to the service desk, where it gets reimaged before it goes back on the network. This applies even if it was only locked and never wiped. Cancel the replacement request if it hasn't shipped yet, and set the asset back to ACTIVE instead of LOST/STOLEN.
stages: Open a DEVICE-LOSS ticket and record the user's account of the loss
Look up the device in the asset inventory and check its encryption status
Force a password reset and revoke all active sessions and tokens for the user
Send a remote lock (or remote wipe if not confirmed encrypted with escrowed key) from the MDM console
Notify the Privacy Office if the device was not confirmed encrypted
Monitor the MDM console for device check-in and confirm the lock
Collect the police report number from the user if the device was stolen
Submit a replacement device request to IT procurement and link it to the ticket
Mark the asset LOST or STOLEN in inventory and close the ticket

decisions.question: Is the device confirmed encrypted with its key escrowed?
branches: Yes: send a remote lock and follow the standard path
No (not encrypted, unknown, or key not escrowed): skip the lock, send a remote wipe immediately, and email the Privacy Office with the ticket number for a possible-data-exposure review

decisions.question: Did the locked device check in to MDM within 24 hours of the lock command?
branches: Yes: lock is confirmed and processing continues
No: queue a remote wipe anyway and note it in the ticket

decisions.question: Was the device stolen or lost?
branches: Stolen: user must file a police report and provide the report number; ticket is on hold and no replacement is ordered until it is received
Lost: no police report needed; proceed to order the replacement

edge_cases: Stolen-device user does not provide the police report number within 5 business days: send a reminder copying their manager and keep the ticket on hold

Device is recovered after the process has started: user must bring it to the service desk for reimaging before it reconnects (even if it was only locked); cancel the replacement request if not yet shipped and set the asset back to ACTIVE

trace_questions.question: What happens if a user reports their laptop stolen and the asset record shows it encrypted but with the key not escrowed?
trace_questions.answer: It is treated as unencrypted: after the password reset and session revocation, the lock is skipped and a remote wipe is sent immediately, and the Privacy Office is emailed with the ticket number for a possible-data-exposure review. Because it was stolen, the ticket goes on hold until the user provides a police report number. No replacement is ordered until then, and the manager is copied on a reminder if it takes more than 5 business days.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a lost, encrypted-and-escrowed laptop does not check in within 24 hours of the lock, and the user finds it two days later before the replacement has shipped?
trace_questions.answer: At the 24-hour mark a remote wipe is queued anyway and noted in the ticket. Since it was lost, no police report was needed and the replacement was requested. When the device is found, the user cannot log back in on it. They must bring it to the service desk to be reimaged before it goes back on the network. The replacement request is cancelled because it has not shipped, and the asset is set back to ACTIVE instead of LOST.

title: Internship-for-Credit Approval at Westbrook State University, Dept. of Communication
workflow_text:
Notes for whoever covers the internship desk while I'm out (fall term). This is the INT 390 for-credit process, NOT the career center job board stuff.

Starts when the student submits the Learning Agreement in the portal. Usually they've already landed the internship. Don't let them tell you the employer 'already said it's fine', we still verify.

First thing: eligibility. Pull their audit. Need 2.5 GPA AND 60+ earned credits. If they miss either one, don't reject outright. They can petition the dept chair (form's in the shared drive, 'Chair Petition INT'). Chair says yes -> carry on like normal. Chair says no -> application is closed, email them the denial template, they can reapply next term.

Oh, before you send anything to the employer: check the Approved Sites list (spreadsheet tab 2). If the company is on it, go straight to sending the Site Verification form to the supervisor. If NOT on it, you have to do the vetting call with the employer first (checklist on tab 3: real supervisor, actual duties, no 100% coffee-run nonsense). Vetting passes -> add them to the list, then send the verification form. Fails -> app is rejected, tell the student why, they can bring a different site.

Supervisor has 10 business days to return the verification form. If nothing by then, send ONE reminder. Still nothing 5 business days after the reminder -> put the app on hold and ask the student for an alternate contact at the site. Restart the 10 days with the new person.

After the verification form is back, forward the Learning Agreement to the faculty sponsor so they can review the learning objectives. Sponsor either approves or sends it back. Sent back -> student revises objectives and resubmits, back to sponsor again. Students get 2 revision rounds. If the sponsor rejects it a third time, stop the email ping-pong and set up an in-person meeting between student and sponsor; they finalize objectives there.

Once approved, I register the student in INT 390. Watch the calendar: if we're past add/drop, it has to go on a Late Add form and the registrar has to sign it, otherwise the reg just bounces.

Mid-term: supervisor fills out the midterm eval (system sends it automatically week 7). Satisfactory -> nothing to do. Unsatisfactory -> schedule a three-way meeting (student, supervisor, sponsor), write up an improvement plan, internship continues.

End of term: student submits final reflection paper, supervisor submits final eval. Then sponsor assigns Pass/Fail. If either the paper or the supervisor eval isn't in by the grade deadline, sponsor enters an Incomplete instead and we chase it next term.

Coordinator checks eligibility (GPA and credits)
Coordinator checks employer against Approved Sites list
Coordinator conducts employer vetting call (if site not on list)
Coordinator sends Site Verification form to supervisor
Supervisor returns Site Verification form
Coordinator forwards Learning Agreement to faculty sponsor
Faculty sponsor reviews learning objectives
Coordinator registers student in INT 390
Supervisor completes midterm evaluation
Student submits final reflection paper
Supervisor submits final evaluation
Faculty sponsor assigns Pass/Fail grade

branches: Yes: proceed to Approved Sites check
No: student may petition dept chair; chair approves -> proceed normally; chair denies -> application closed, denial email sent, may reapply next term

decisions.question: Is the employer on the Approved Sites list?
branches: Yes: send Site Verification form to supervisor
No: conduct vetting call; passes -> add to list and send verification form; fails -> application rejected, student may bring a different site

decisions.question: Does the faculty sponsor approve the learning objectives?
branches: Yes: register student in INT 390
No: student revises and resubmits to sponsor (up to 2 revision rounds); on third rejection, in-person student-sponsor meeting to finalize objectives

decisions.question: Is the midterm evaluation satisfactory?
branches: Yes: no action, internship continues
No: three-way meeting (student, supervisor, sponsor), improvement plan written, internship continues

branches: Yes: sponsor assigns Pass/Fail
No: sponsor enters Incomplete, materials chased next term

Sponsor rejects objectives a third time (after 2 revision rounds): email revisions stop and an in-person student-sponsor meeting finalizes objectives
Approval comes after add/drop deadline: registration requires Late Add form signed by the registrar

trace_questions.question: What happens if a student has a 2.3 GPA, the chair approves the petition, and the employer is not on the Approved Sites list but passes the vetting call?
trace_questions.answer: The student proceeds after chair approval; the coordinator adds the employer to the Approved Sites list and then sends the Site Verification form to the supervisor, continuing the normal process.

trace_questions.question: What happens if the supervisor never responds to the verification form, even after the reminder?
trace_questions.answer: After 10 business days one reminder is sent; if there is still no response 5 business days after the reminder, the application is put on hold and the student is asked for an alternate contact at the site, with the 10-day window restarting for the new contact.

title: Transfer Credit Evaluation for Incoming Transfer Students
workflow_text:
TC eval notes (for whoever is covering while I'm out)

Quick heads up first: the cap is 64 transfer credits, period. Once everything is entered in degree audit, look at the total. Over 64? Trim elective credit first until it's at 64, and note what got dropped in the report. Don't trim direct equivalents unless there's literally no elective credit left to cut. Under 64, nothing to do.

OK, actual flow:

Transcripts land in the TC shared inbox. Pull it, open a row in the tracker sheet (student ID, sending school, date received).

Check it's official: e-delivered through the transcript service OR scanned from a sealed envelope (mailroom stamps those). Student-uploaded PDFs / unofficial printouts don't count.
- not official -> email student the 'official copy needed' template, set tracker status to HOLD. Nothing else gets done on the file.
- if 30 days go by on HOLD with no official copy, close the row as INCOMPLETE and send the closure email. They have to resubmit from scratch.

Then go course by course. Grade screen BEFORE you bother looking anything up:
- below C- = not transferable, mark it and move on
- C- or better... BUT check whether the course would count as a prereq for their declared major (prereq list is on the dept tab). If it does, they need a C or better. A C- in a major prereq only gets general elective credit -> mark as elective, skip the lookup for that one.
- non-prereq courses at C- or above go on to lookup.

Lookup = equivalency table. If there's a match AND it was reviewed in the last 5 years, just apply it. No match, or the match is older than 5 years -> email the student for the syllabus, then route course + syllabus to the dept's faculty reviewer (list on the contacts tab).

Faculty comes back with one of: direct equivalent, elective credit, no credit, or 'need more info.' More info -> go back to the student for whatever they asked (usually course schedule or sample assignments), send it back to the same reviewer. Two rounds max. If they're still asking after the 2nd round, it defaults to elective credit and we stop.
Also: if a reviewer hasn't answered in 10 business days, escalate to the dept chair and the chair makes the call.

After every course has a result, enter all of it into degree audit, then do the 64 check (top of these notes).

Email the transfer credit report to student + their assigned advisor.

Last thing: any new faculty or chair rulings get added to the equivalency table with today's date so we don't re-review them. Defaulted electives from the 2-round thing do NOT go in the table since nobody actually ruled on them. Then close the tracker row as COMPLETE.
stages: Pull transcript from the TC shared inbox and open a tracker row
Verify the transcript is official
Screen each course's grade (including major-prerequisite check)
Look up eligible courses in the equivalency table
Apply current equivalencies (reviewed within 5 years)
Request syllabus from the student for unmatched or outdated courses
Route course and syllabus to the department faculty reviewer
Enter all course evaluations into degree audit
Check total transfer credits against the 64-credit cap
Email the transfer credit report to the student and advisor
Add new faculty/chair rulings to the equivalency table
Close the tracker row as COMPLETE

decisions.question: Is the transcript official (e-delivered via transcript service or scanned from a sealed envelope)?
branches: Yes: proceed to course-by-course evaluation
No: email student the 'official copy needed' template and set file to HOLD; no further work until official copy arrives

decisions.question: Does the course grade meet the transfer threshold?
branches: Below C-: course is not transferable
C- or better and not a major prerequisite: proceed to equivalency lookup
C- or better and a major prerequisite (nested check): C or better proceeds to lookup; C- receives general elective credit only and skips lookup

decisions.question: Is there a matching equivalency in the table reviewed within the last 5 years?
branches: Yes: apply the existing equivalency
No match or match older than 5 years: request syllabus from student and route to department faculty reviewer

decisions.question: What does the faculty reviewer decide?
branches: Direct equivalent: record as equivalent
Elective credit: record as elective
No credit: record as not transferable
Need more info: request materials from student and resend to the same reviewer (max 2 rounds, then default to elective credit)

decisions.question: Does the total transfer credit exceed 64?
branches: Yes: trim elective credit first down to 64 (direct equivalents only if no elective credit remains) and note dropped credits in the report
No: no change

edge_cases: Transcript stays on HOLD for 30 days without an official copy: tracker row is closed as INCOMPLETE, closure email sent, and student must resubmit from scratch
Faculty reviewer requests more info more than twice: after the second round the course defaults to elective credit, and that default is not added to the equivalency table
Faculty reviewer does not respond within 10 business days: escalate to the department chair, who makes the ruling

trace_questions.question: What happens if a student earned a C- in a course that counts as a prerequisite for their declared major, and the equivalency table has a current match for it?
trace_questions.answer: The C- clears the general C- threshold, but because the course is a major prerequisite it needs a C or better. It is marked as general elective credit only and the equivalency lookup is skipped, so the current match is not applied. The elective credit is entered in degree audit and is first in line to be trimmed if the total exceeds 64.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a course passes the grade screen, has no equivalency table match, and the faculty reviewer asks for more information in both rounds?
trace_questions.answer: The student is asked for the syllabus and the course goes to the department faculty reviewer. Each 'need more info' request sends staff back to the student for materials, which are returned to the same reviewer. After the second round, if the reviewer is still asking, the course defaults to elective credit and review stops. It is entered in degree audit, subject to the 64-credit cap check, and included in the report, but it is not added to the equivalency table because no one actually ruled on it.

title: Intern Weekly Timesheet and Stipend Processing at Harborview Health Network
workflow_text:
Intern timesheets - how we process them (for whoever covers for me while I'm out)

All our paid interns log hours weekly in the staff portal. Here's the flow:

- Intern enters their hours for the week and hits Submit. Due Fri by 5pm.
- Portal pings their site supervisor, who reviews the hours against the schedule.
- If the hours look right, the supervisor approves and it lands in our HR queue. If something's off (wrong dates, missing shift, etc.), the supervisor sends it back with a comment. The intern fixes it and resubmits, and it goes back to the supervisor for another review. This can bounce more than once, which is fine.

Once it's in the HR queue:
- Check total hours vs. the 20 hr/week cap in the intern agreement. 20 or under = good to go. Over 20 = do NOT export yet. Forward it to the Internship Program Manager for sign-off first. Once she signs, it's good to go.
- Export all good-to-go timesheets to payroll by Mon 12 noon. This is a hard cutoff.
- Payroll pays the stipend on the next pay date (usually Thurs).
- Last step: send the intern the standard confirmation email (template is in the shared drive under Intern Comms) with hours paid and pay date.

Heads up: anything not ready to export by Mon noon (late submission, still bouncing with the supervisor, waiting on PM sign-off, whatever) just rolls into the following week's export. It gets paid on the pay date after that. Don't try to sneak it in after the cutoff. If the intern asks, let them know it'll be in the next cycle.
stages: Intern enters weekly hours and submits timesheet in the portal by Friday 5pm
Site supervisor reviews hours against the schedule
Supervisor approves timesheet and it moves to the HR queue
HR coordinator checks total hours against the 20 hr/week cap
HR coordinator exports good-to-go timesheets to payroll by Monday 12 noon
Payroll pays the stipend on the next pay date
HR coordinator emails the intern a confirmation with hours paid and pay date

decisions.question: Do the submitted hours look correct to the site supervisor?
branches: Yes: supervisor approves and the timesheet goes to the HR queue
No: supervisor returns it with a comment; intern corrects and resubmits, and it goes back to the supervisor for review (may repeat)

decisions.question: Are the total weekly hours over the 20-hour cap?
branches: No (20 or under): timesheet is good to go for export
Yes (over 20): HR forwards it to the Internship Program Manager for sign-off before export; once signed, it is good to go

edge_cases: Any timesheet not ready to export by the Monday 12 noon cutoff (late submission, still being returned/resubmitted, or awaiting Program Manager sign-off) rolls into the following week's export and is paid on the pay date after that; it must not be added after the cutoff.

trace_questions.question: What happens if the supervisor sends an intern's timesheet back for a missing shift, and the intern doesn't resubmit until Tuesday morning?
trace_questions.answer: The corrected timesheet goes back to the supervisor for review. Because it wasn't ready by the Monday noon cutoff, it rolls into the following week's export and is paid on the pay date after that. The intern can be told it will be in the next cycle.

trace_questions.question: What happens if the supervisor approves a timesheet showing 23 hours and the Program Manager signs off Monday at 10am?
trace_questions.answer: Because 23 hours exceeds the 20-hour cap, HR forwards it to the Internship Program Manager for sign-off instead of exporting it. Once she signs at 10am, it is good to go and is exported before the Monday noon cutoff. Payroll then pays the stipend on the next pay date, and HR sends the intern the confirmation email.

title: Handling a User-Reported Phishing Email
workflow_text:
Phish reports - how we work them (for whoever's covering my shift)

Reports come in two ways: the Report Phish button in the mail client, which auto-creates a ticket in the desk queue with the original message attached, or someone just forwards it to the helpdesk inbox. If it's a forward, open the ticket yourself and ask them to resend as an attachment, because a forward strips the headers and we need those.

Before you do anything clever, check the sender against the allowlist (vendor list tab in the shared sheet). A ton of reports are just our own HR survey tool or the payroll provider. If it's on the list, close as "Not phishing", send the reporter the "thanks, this one's legit" template, and you're done.

Not on the list -> drop the links/attachments into the sandbox. NEVER click from your own machine. Sandbox gives you a verdict:
- clean but junky (newsletter, cold sales pitch) = add a spam rule for the sender, reply to the reporter, close.
- malicious or suspicious = keep going.

Oh, and important: if the reporter is in Finance or is an exec, and the email is asking for a payment / bank detail change / gift cards, skip the queue. Call Security Ops and the Finance manager straight away, then carry on with the rest of this in parallel.

For malicious ones:
* search mail logs for everyone else who got the same message (subject + sender)
* if it's more than 25 recipients, that's a campaign - page the SecOps on-call. You still do the purge and block yourself, don't wait for them.
* purge the message from all mailboxes with the admin purge tool. Shared mailboxes sometimes fail the purge - if so, ask the mailbox owner's admin to delete it manually and note who you asked in the ticket.
* block the sender domain and any URLs at the mail gateway.

Then message every recipient (not just the reporter) asking if they clicked anything.
 - didn't touch it: note it, nothing else.
 - clicked the link: ask if they typed in a password. If no, kick off a remote AV scan on their device and note it. If yes -> force password reset and revoke all their active sessions.
 - opened the attachment: isolate the device from the network via the endpoint console and escalate to SecOps as P1. Don't try to clean it yourself.

People don't always answer. Give it 4 hours, chase once by chat/phone. Still nothing by end of day -> check the proxy logs for that user hitting the bad URL. Proxy hit = treat it like they entered credentials (reset + revoke). No hit = note "no response, no proxy hit" and move on.

Once everyone's accounted for, post a short awareness note in the staff channel (screenshot with links blurred), update the ticket with what you did, and close it.
stages: Receive the phishing report and open a ticket (ask for resend as attachment if forwarded)
Check the sender against the allowlist
Analyze links and attachments in the sandbox
Search mail logs for other recipients of the same message
Purge the message from all mailboxes
Block the sender domain and URLs at the mail gateway
Contact every recipient to ask whether they interacted with the email
Run remote AV scan, or reset password and revoke sessions, or isolate device and escalate, based on each response
Chase non-responders and check proxy logs if still no answer
Post an awareness note in the staff channel
Update the ticket with actions taken and close it

decisions.question: Is the sender on the allowlist?
branches: Yes: close as 'Not phishing', send the reporter the legit template, done
No: send links/attachments to the sandbox

decisions.question: What is the sandbox verdict?
branches: Clean but junky: add a spam rule for the sender, reply to the reporter, close
Malicious or suspicious: continue to recipient search, purge, and block

decisions.question: Did the message go to more than 25 recipients?
branches: Yes: treat as a campaign and page the SecOps on-call, but still do the purge and block yourself
No: proceed with purge and block without paging

decisions.question: How did each recipient interact with the email?
branches: Didn't touch it: note it, no further action
Clicked the link: ask if they entered a password - if no, run a remote AV scan and note it; if yes, force a password reset and revoke all active sessions
Opened the attachment: isolate the device via the endpoint console and escalate to SecOps as P1

decisions.question: For a recipient with no response by end of day, does the proxy log show them hitting the bad URL?
branches: Yes: treat as credentials entered (password reset + revoke sessions)
No: note 'no response, no proxy hit' and move on

edge_cases: Reporter is in Finance or an exec and the email requests a payment, bank detail change, or gift cards: call Security Ops and the Finance manager immediately, then continue the normal process in parallel
Purge fails on a shared mailbox: ask the mailbox owner's admin to delete it manually and record who was asked in the ticket
Recipient doesn't respond: wait 4 hours, chase once by chat/phone, and if still nothing by end of day, check proxy logs to decide whether to treat as compromised

trace_questions.question: What happens if the sender isn't allowlisted, the sandbox says malicious, the message went to 40 people, and one recipient says they clicked the link but didn't type a password?
trace_questions.answer: Search the mail logs, page the SecOps on-call because it exceeds 25 recipients (a campaign), but still purge the message and block the domain/URLs yourself. Message all recipients; for the one who clicked without entering a password, kick off a remote AV scan on their device and note it in the ticket. After everyone is accounted for, post the awareness note, update and close the ticket.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a recipient of a confirmed malicious email never replies to the 'did you click?' message?
trace_questions.answer: Wait 4 hours, then chase them once by chat or phone. If there's still no response by end of day, check the proxy logs: if they hit the bad URL, treat it as credentials entered and force a password reset plus revoke all sessions; if there's no proxy hit, note 'no response, no proxy hit' and move on to the awareness note and closing the ticket.

title: Student Club Room Reservation Requests
workflow_text:
Notes for covering the room request inbox (Student Activities Office, Northfield University)

Club room requests come in through the Student Activities portal. Each one lands in the shared queue with the club name, event date/time, room wanted, and expected headcount. Try to work through them in order received.

First thing, open the Club Roster sheet and confirm the club is listed as ACTIVE for this term. If it shows INACTIVE or isn't on the roster at all, don't go any further. Reply using the "Club Not Active" template, which includes the re-registration link, and mark the request Rejected in the portal. They'll need to re-register and then submit a new request.

If the club is active:
- Look up the requested room and time slot in the campus scheduling system (RoomBook).
- Room is free → put a tentative hold on it under the club's name.
- Room is already booked → don't hold anything yet. Find up to 2 comparable rooms (similar size) that are open at the same time and email those options to the club officer. Once they pick one, place the tentative hold on that room and carry on as normal.
  * If the officer doesn't reply within 3 business days, release nothing (there's no hold) and just close the request in the portal as "No Response." They'd have to start over with a new request.

After the hold is placed, email the officer the confirmation template with the Room Use Agreement attached (no-food rules, cleanup expectations, etc.).

When the signed agreement comes back, switch the RoomBook hold from tentative to confirmed.

Last step: log the booking in the Club Events Tracker spreadsheet (club, room, date, headcount) and mark the portal request Complete.
stages: Receive room request from the Student Activities portal queue
Verify club status on the Club Roster sheet
Check requested room and time slot availability in RoomBook
Place a tentative hold on the room under the club's name
Email the officer the confirmation with the Room Use Agreement attached
Change the RoomBook hold from tentative to confirmed after the signed agreement is returned
Log the booking in the Club Events Tracker and mark the portal request Complete

decisions.question: Is the club listed as ACTIVE for the current term on the Club Roster?
branches: Yes: proceed to check room availability in RoomBook
No (inactive or not listed): send the "Club Not Active" template with the re-registration link, mark the request Rejected, and stop; the club must re-register and submit a new request

decisions.question: Is the requested room free at the requested time in RoomBook?
branches: Yes: place a tentative hold on the requested room
No: email the officer up to 2 comparable open rooms; once they choose one, place the tentative hold on that room and continue

edge_cases: If the officer does not reply to the alternative-room options within 3 business days, the request is closed in the portal as "No Response" (no hold exists to release) and the club must submit a new request.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a request comes in from a club that does not appear on the Club Roster at all?
trace_questions.answer: Processing stops immediately without checking room availability. Staff reply with the "Club Not Active" template including the re-registration link and mark the request Rejected in the portal. The club must re-register and then submit a new request.

trace_questions.question: What happens if an active club requests a room that is already booked and the officer never responds to the alternative options?
trace_questions.answer: Staff place no hold, find up to 2 comparable open rooms, and email them to the officer. After 3 business days with no reply, the request is closed in the portal as "No Response"; nothing needs to be released, and the club would have to start over with a new request.

title: Working an Impossible-Travel Sign-In Alert
workflow_text:
Impossible travel alerts - how I work them (night shift notes for Priya)

These land in the SIEM queue tagged IMPTRAVEL. Open the alert and grab the username, both source IPs, the geo for each, and the timestamps. Paste it all into the ticket, you'll need it later.

First thing: check both IPs against the egress list (wiki > NetOps > Known Egress). Our VPN concentrators exit from two different countries, so half of these are just someone flipping VPN regions. If either IP is on the egress list, OR the user has an approved entry in the HR travel sheet covering that country, close as benign and tag FP-KNOWN. Done.
NB the travel sheet only counts if the country matches. Someone approved for Germany who signs in from Brazil is NOT covered, so keep going.

Otherwise reach out to the user. Use Teams or phone, never email (if the account is popped, the attacker reads your email). Ask whether both sign-ins were them.
- they confirm both -> close benign, tag FP-USER, add a line about what they told you (personal VPN, hotel wifi, whatever)
- they say no or aren't sure -> contain (see below)
- no answer within 30 min -> treat it as a no and contain. Don't sit on it.
