Oh, and before you even message them, check whether the account is in the Privileged group (domain admins, finance approvers, exec assistants). If it is, don't wait on the user. Contain right away and ping the IR lead on the on-call line at the same time. You can still contact the user afterwards for the ticket.

Containment = revoke all sessions in the identity portal, THEN force a password reset + MFA re-registration. Order matters. Revoke first, otherwise they keep a token.

After containment, pull the mailbox rules and OAuth app consents for the last 7 days.
- nothing weird -> block the unfamiliar IP in conditional access, write up the ticket, close as contained
- forwarding rules / sketchy app consent -> delete them, then open a Sev2 incident and hand it to the IR lead. If the forwarding rule pointed at an external address AND the message trace shows mail actually went out, also notify the privacy officer (template is in the IR folder). If the rule existed but the trace shows nothing sent, just note that in the incident. No privacy notice.

One more thing: if the same user throws another IMPTRAVEL within 24h of you resetting them, don't restart triage from the top. Skip the egress check and the user check, revoke sessions again, and go straight to a Sev2 with the IR lead. That usually means a persistence mechanism we missed.
stages: Pull alert details (username, source IPs, geo, timestamps) from the SIEM and record them in the ticket
Check both source IPs against the known egress list and the HR travel sheet
Check whether the account is in the Privileged group
Contact the user via Teams or phone to confirm the sign-ins
Revoke all active sessions in the identity portal
Force a password reset and MFA re-registration
Review mailbox rules and OAuth app consents for the last 7 days
Delete malicious forwarding rules or app consents
Open a Sev2 incident and hand it to the IR lead
Check the message trace and notify the privacy officer if mail went out externally
Block the unfamiliar IP in conditional access
Document the ticket and close it

decisions.question: Is either IP on the known egress list, or does the user have approved travel covering that country?
branches: Yes: close as benign and tag FP-KNOWN
No (including approved travel to a different country): continue triage

decisions.question: Is the account in the Privileged group (domain admins, finance approvers, exec assistants)?
branches: Yes: contain immediately without waiting for the user and ping the IR lead on the on-call line; the user can be contacted afterwards for the ticket
No: contact the user via Teams or phone and wait for a response

decisions.question: How does the user respond about the sign-ins?
branches: Confirms both: close as benign, tag FP-USER, and note their explanation
Says no or is unsure: proceed to containment
No answer within 30 minutes: treat as a no and proceed to containment

decisions.question: Does the mailbox and OAuth review show suspicious forwarding rules or app consents?
branches: No: block the unfamiliar IP in conditional access, document, and close as contained
Yes: delete them, open a Sev2 incident, and hand it to the IR lead

decisions.question: (Nested, only if forwarding rules were found) Did the rule forward to an external address AND does the message trace show mail actually went out?
branches: Yes: also notify the privacy officer using the IR folder template
No (rule existed but nothing was sent): note this in the incident, no privacy notice

edge_cases: Approved travel only counts if the country matches; a sign-in from a country other than the approved one is not covered and triage continues
If the user doesn't respond within 30 minutes, the alert is treated as unconfirmed and containment proceeds

Loop: if the same user triggers another IMPTRAVEL alert within 24 hours of being reset, skip the egress and user checks, revoke sessions again, and go straight to a Sev2 with the IR lead (likely a missed persistence mechanism)
Sessions must be revoked before the password and MFA reset, otherwise the attacker keeps a valid token

trace_questions.question: What happens if a non-privileged user's sign-in IPs aren't on the egress list, they have no travel entry, they don't reply within 30 minutes, and the mailbox review finds a forwarding rule to an external address but the message trace shows nothing was sent?
trace_questions.answer: The 30-minute silence is treated as a no, so the analyst contains: revoke all sessions first, then force a password reset and MFA re-registration. The mailbox review finds the forwarding rule, so the analyst deletes it, opens a Sev2 incident, and hands it to the IR lead. Because the trace shows no mail actually went out, the analyst only notes that in the incident. No privacy officer notification is sent.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a user who was contained and reset earlier the same day (with a clean mailbox review) triggers another IMPTRAVEL alert 6 hours later?
trace_questions.answer: Because it is within 24 hours of the reset, the analyst does not restart triage. They skip the egress/travel check and the user confirmation, revoke the user's sessions again, and go straight to opening a Sev2 incident with the IR lead, since this usually indicates a missed persistence mechanism.

title: Shared Drive Folder Access Requests
workflow_text:
Quick notes for covering the folder access queue while I'm out.

These come in through the portal under "Shared Drive Access". When one lands, check the ticket has the full folder path and whether they want read-only or edit. If either is missing, reply on the ticket and ask; don't guess.

Next, look up the folder in the Folder Owner Register (the spreadsheet pinned in the team channel). Every top-level share has a named owner, usually a dept head or their delegate.

Email the owner using the "Access Approval" template and paste the ticket number in the subject line. Set the ticket to Pending Approval.

When the owner replies:
- Approved: go ahead and grant it (see below).
- Denied: put the owner's reason in the ticket, let the user know, and close it as Denied. Do NOT grant anything, even if the user pushes back. They can take it up with the owner directly.

Granting: we never add people straight onto folder permissions. Add them to the AD group for that folder instead.
- read-only -> the folder's _Read group
- edit -> the folder's _Modify group
If the owner approved a different level than the user asked for, go with what the owner approved.

Then tell the user to sign out and back in (group changes don't show up until they do) and ask them to confirm they can open the folder. Once they confirm, close the ticket as Resolved.

Owners going quiet: if there's no reply after 3 business days, send one reminder. If there's still nothing by end of day 5, escalate to the owner's line manager with the same template. The manager can approve or deny on the owner's behalf, and you treat their answer exactly like the owner's.
stages: Receive the access request ticket from the portal and confirm the folder path and access level are provided
Look up the folder owner in the Folder Owner Register
Email the owner for approval using the Access Approval template and set the ticket to Pending Approval
Add the user to the folder's _Read or _Modify AD group
Ask the user to sign out and back in and confirm they can open the folder
Close the ticket as Resolved

decisions.question: Does the folder owner approve the request?
branches: Approved: proceed to grant access via the AD group
Denied: record the owner's reason, notify the user, and close the ticket as Denied without granting access

decisions.question: What access level did the owner approve?
branches: Read-only: add the user to the folder's _Read group
Edit: add the user to the folder's _Modify group

edge_cases: Owner does not reply: after 3 business days send one reminder; if still no reply by end of day 5, escalate to the owner's line manager, whose approval or denial is treated the same as the owner's

trace_questions.question: What happens if a user requests edit access and the folder owner approves only read-only access?
trace_questions.answer: The help desk follows the owner's approval and adds the user to the folder's _Read group, not the _Modify group. The user is then told to sign out and back in and confirm they can open the folder, after which the ticket is closed as Resolved.

trace_questions.question: What happens if the folder owner hasn't replied after 3 business days and still hasn't replied by the end of day 5 after a reminder?
trace_questions.answer: The request is escalated to the owner's line manager using the same Access Approval template. If the manager approves, access is granted through the appropriate AD group and the normal sign-out/confirm/close steps follow. If the manager denies, the reason is recorded, the user is notified, and the ticket is closed as Denied.

title: Intern Return-Offer Review at Lakeshore Engineering Partners
workflow_text:
Return offer review - notes for Dana while I'm out

This kicks off around week 8 of the summer program. Goal is to get every intern either an offer, a decline, or parked by end of program.

Evals
- Final eval forms are in the HR portal (Talent > Intern Evals). Managers fill them out; we just chase.
- Deadline for managers is Friday of week 9. Anyone missing on Monday: email the manager AND cc their director. They get 3 more business days.
- Still nothing after that? Mark the intern "no recommendation" in the tracker. They drop out of this cycle, and we revisit them in the fall review. Do NOT send them a decline letter. They haven't been declined.

Sorting
- Overall rating 4 or 5: straight onto the committee list.
- Rating 3: ping the manager and ask point blank if they want to hire. Yes means add to the committee list with a note ("mgr confirmed, rating 3"). No means decline path.
- Rating 1 or 2: decline path, no committee.

Before committee
- Send Finance the committee list grouped by dept and ask about open entry-level headcount for next year. They usually turn it around in 2 days.
- If a dept has no headcount, the intern still goes to committee, but flag them "pipeline." The committee can only give pipeline folks a deferred offer, meaning a start date next year pending budget. No regular offer.
- Put together the packets (eval + manager comments + headcount status). The usual format is fine.

Committee
- Meets the Tuesday of week 10. They approve or reject each person. Rejected goes to the decline path.
- For approved interns, draft the offer from the template. Use the standard or deferred version depending on the flag. Recruiting lead (Marcus) signs. Send it through the portal. The intern has 14 days to accept.
- Accepted: hand off to the new-hire onboarding team. Our part is done.
- No response by day 14: recruiter calls once. If still nothing 2 days after that, the offer lapses. Log it as "lapsed" in the tracker.

Decline path
- Manager has the conversation with the intern first. Always. Don't send anything until they confirm it happened.
- Then send the standard thank-you letter and add them to the alumni talent pool so they get future postings.
stages: Collect final evaluation forms from managers in the HR portal
Review overall ratings and sort interns into committee list or decline path
Confirm next-year entry-level headcount with Finance for each department
Assemble committee packets (eval, manager comments, headcount status)
Present candidates to the conversion committee for approve/reject
Draft offer letter (standard or deferred) from template
Get recruiting lead signature and send offer via portal with 14-day acceptance window
Track acceptance and hand accepted interns off to new-hire onboarding
Decline path: manager holds conversation, then send thank-you letter and add intern to alumni talent pool

decisions.question: What is the intern's overall evaluation rating?
branches: 4 or 5: added directly to the committee list
3: manager is asked whether they want to hire. If yes, the intern is added to the committee list with a note. If no, the intern goes to the decline path
1 or 2: decline path with no committee review

decisions.question: Does the intern's department have open entry-level headcount for next year?
branches: Yes: intern goes to committee eligible for a standard offer
No: intern still goes to committee but is flagged 'pipeline' and can only receive a deferred offer (next-year start pending budget)

decisions.question: Does the conversion committee approve the intern?
branches: Approved: offer drafted (standard or deferred per flag), signed by the recruiting lead, and sent via portal
Rejected: decline path (manager conversation, thank-you letter, alumni talent pool)

edge_cases: Manager misses the Friday week-9 eval deadline: the manager and their director are emailed and given 3 more business days. If there is still no eval, the intern is marked 'no recommendation', drops out of this cycle, is revisited in the fall review, and is not sent a decline letter.
Intern doesn't respond to the offer within 14 days: the recruiter calls once. If there is no response 2 days after that, the offer lapses and is logged as 'lapsed' in the tracker.

trace_questions.question: What happens if an intern receives an overall rating of 3, the manager confirms they want to hire, the department has no open headcount, and the committee approves?
trace_questions.answer: The intern is added to the committee list with a note that the manager confirmed despite a rating of 3, and is flagged 'pipeline' because there's no headcount. After committee approval, they get a deferred offer (next-year start pending budget) drafted from the template, signed by the recruiting lead, and sent through the portal with a 14-day acceptance window.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a manager hasn't submitted the final eval by Friday of week 9 and still hasn't submitted it 3 business days after the follow-up email?
trace_questions.answer: The intern is marked 'no recommendation' in the tracker and drops out of this cycle, to be revisited in the fall review. No decline letter is sent, because the intern has not been declined.

title: Instructor Grade Change Request Processing
workflow_text:
Grade change requests: how we handle them at the Registrar's front desk

Grade change forms come into the records@ shared inbox, usually as PDFs, sometimes a scan from the dept office. Log each one in the tracker sheet the day it arrives (student ID, course, term, old grade, new grade, date received). Each row is the ticket.

First look at the form itself:
- Need the instructor signature AND the dept chair signature. The reason box has to be filled in too. "Per discussion" is NOT a reason.
- If anything's missing, reply to the instructor with what's missing, mark the ticket "returned" and put the date. They have 10 business days to send it back fixed. If nothing comes back by then, close the ticket as "expired." If they send it later, it's a brand new request: new row, start over from the top. Don't reopen the old one.

Once the form is complete, check the term. If the course term ended more than 1 year ago, it needs the Dean of Academic Affairs to sign off. Forward it to the dean's office queue and set the ticket to "pending dean." They usually take about a week.
- Dean approves: carry on as normal.
- Dean denies: email the instructor with the dean's note and close the ticket as "denied." Nothing goes in the SIS. We don't contact the student; that's the instructor's job.
Anything 1 year or less goes straight through, no dean.

Pull up the student in the SIS and confirm the old grade on the form matches what's actually on the record. Mismatches are usually a wrong section number, so call the dept office to sort it out.

HEADS UP: if the student has already graduated and the degree is posted, the record is locked. You can't enter the change yourself. Send it to the Associate Registrar for an override. They make the entry, and then it comes back to you for the rest.

Enter the new grade in SIS with the change reason code. Then run the standing recalculation (GPA + academic standing). If the student's standing changed, e.g. came off probation, dropped below 2.0, or now qualifies for dean's list, forward the ticket to the Advising Office so they can update holds and outreach. If nothing changed, skip that.

Send the standard notice email to the student and instructor (template "GC-Complete"). Then save the signed PDF in the student's folder in the records archive and close the ticket as "processed."
stages: Receive grade change form in the shared inbox
Log the request in the tracker sheet
Review the form for both signatures and a valid reason
Check whether the course term ended more than one year ago
Route to the Dean of Academic Affairs for approval when required
Verify the old grade against the student record in the SIS
Enter the new grade in the SIS with the change reason code
Run the GPA and academic standing recalculation
Notify the student and instructor with the GC-Complete email
File the signed form in the records archive and close the ticket

decisions.question: Is the form complete, with instructor signature, chair signature, and a valid reason?
branches: Yes: proceed to the term check
No: return the form to the instructor, mark the ticket returned, and start the 10-business-day clock

decisions.question: Did the course term end more than one year ago?
branches: Yes: forward to the dean's office; if the dean approves, continue processing; if the dean denies, email the instructor the dean's note and close the ticket as denied with no SIS change
No: proceed directly to the SIS verification without dean approval

decisions.question: Did the student's academic standing change after the recalculation?
branches: Yes: forward the ticket to the Advising Office, then send notices and file
No: skip Advising and go straight to notices and filing

edge_cases: Returned form not resubmitted within 10 business days: the ticket is closed as expired, and any later submission is logged as a new request starting from the beginning
Student has already graduated with the degree posted: the record is locked, so the Associate Registrar must enter the change via override before the remaining steps continue
Old grade on the form does not match the SIS record: call the department office to resolve it (usually a wrong section number)

trace_questions.question: What happens if a complete, fully signed form arrives for a course whose term ended 14 months ago, and the dean denies it?
trace_questions.answer: Because the term ended more than a year ago, it is forwarded to the dean's office and marked pending dean. On denial, the staff member emails the instructor with the dean's note and closes the ticket as denied. No change is entered in the SIS, and the registrar does not contact the student; that is left to the instructor.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a form missing the chair signature is returned to the instructor and the corrected form comes back 12 business days later?
trace_questions.answer: The original ticket would already have been closed as expired after 10 business days. The resubmission is treated as a brand-new request: it gets a new tracker row and starts over from the top, with the form review, the term check, and so on. The old ticket is not reopened.

title: Verifying and Processing an MFA Reset Request at the Help Desk
workflow_text:
MFA reset requests - how we handle them on the desk

These come in by phone most of the time ("got a new phone, authenticator is gone"). Attackers know this is an easy way into an account, so don't skip steps even if the person sounds legit or is in a hurry.

- First thing: open a ticket under category Access > MFA Reset. Put the caller's name, the username they gave, and the callback number they gave in the notes.
- Look the user up in the company directory and get the mobile number on file. Use ONLY the directory number for verification. If the caller asks you to use a different number (traveling, new phone, etc.), note it in the ticket but still use the directory number.
- Hang up and call them back on the directory number.

If nobody picks up on the callback: leave a voicemail (don't mention MFA, just ask them to call the help desk about their ticket number), wait 30 min, try once more. If there's still no answer after the second try, close the ticket as "Unable to verify". They can call in again and we start over.

Once you reach them, ask the two verification questions from the directory record (employee ID + manager's name). 
  - Passes both -> carry on below.
  - Fails either one, or the person who answers says they never asked for a reset -> STOP. Do not reset anything. Set the ticket to "Suspected social engineering" and assign it to the Security Operations queue. They take it from there.

Before resetting, check the account's group membership.
  - Normal user -> go straight to the reset.
  - Anything privileged (domain admin, server admin, finance approver groups) -> you need a second approver from the IAM team. Ping the IAM on-call in the ticket and wait for their approval comment before doing the reset.

Reset steps:
- Clear the user's existing MFA registrations in the identity portal.
- Issue a Temporary Access Pass (valid 8 hrs) and read it to the user on the verified call. Tell them to enroll their new device before it expires.
- Send the standard "Your MFA was reset" email to the user AND their manager. This is so they'll notice if it wasn't them.
- Close the ticket as Resolved.
stages: Open a ticket under Access > MFA Reset with the caller's details
Look up the user's mobile number in the company directory
Call the user back on the directory number
Ask the two verification questions (employee ID and manager's name)
Check the account's group membership for privileged access
Clear existing MFA registrations and issue an 8-hour Temporary Access Pass
Send the MFA reset notification email to the user and their manager
Close the ticket as Resolved

decisions.question: Does the person on the callback pass both verification questions and confirm they requested the reset?
branches: Yes: continue to the group membership check and reset
No (fails either question, or says they never requested a reset): do not reset; mark the ticket 'Suspected social engineering' and assign it to the Security Operations queue

decisions.question: Is the account privileged (domain admin, server admin, or finance approver groups)?
branches: No (normal user): proceed directly to the reset
Yes: ping the IAM on-call and wait for their approval comment in the ticket before performing the reset

edge_cases: The callback to the directory number goes unanswered: leave a voicemail referencing only the ticket number, wait 30 minutes and try once more; if there's still no answer, close the ticket as 'Unable to verify' and the user must call in again to restart.

trace_questions.question: What happens if the user answers the callback, correctly gives their employee ID and manager's name, and their account is in the domain admin group?
trace_questions.answer: Because the account is privileged, the analyst must ping the IAM on-call and wait for an approval comment in the ticket. After approval, the analyst clears the existing MFA registrations, issues an 8-hour Temporary Access Pass on the verified call, emails the user and their manager the reset notification, and closes the ticket as Resolved.

trace_questions.question: What happens if the caller asks to be called back on a new number because they're traveling, but when the analyst calls the directory number the person who answers says they never requested a reset?
trace_questions.answer: The analyst notes the requested number but still uses the directory number. Since the person reached says they never asked for a reset, the analyst stops, does not reset anything, sets the ticket to 'Suspected social engineering', and assigns it to the Security Operations queue.

title: Non-Standard Software Install Requests
workflow_text:
Software install reqs - notes for whoever is covering the queue this week

These come in through the portal under 'Software Request'. First thing: look the title up on the Approved Software List (ASL, pinned on the team wiki).

On the ASL -> no approvals needed. Push it from the deployment console to the user's machine and tag the ticket 'ASL-push'. Then jump to the confirm step at the bottom.

NOT on the ASL -> needs manager sign-off AND a security review, in that order.
- Manager: from the ticket, Actions > Request Approval. This emails the form to the user's manager.
- Mgr gets 3 business days. No answer = send ONE reminder and give 2 more business days. Still nothing -> close as 'Expired - no approval'. Tell the user they can resubmit.
- Mgr declines -> close the ticket and paste their reason into the user-facing note.
- Mgr approves -> reassign to the Security queue. They check license terms and data handling.

Security comes back with one of three answers:
- Cleared -> continue below.
- Rejected -> close, copy their note to the user.
- 'Use alternative' -> they'll name an ASL equivalent. Offer it to the user. If the user takes it, handle it like any ASL request (console push, ASL-push tag). If the user says no, close as rejected.

Cleared items: log the license with Procurement (cost center is on the manager's approval form). Do this even for freeware, they track EULAs. Then book a remote session with the user - they have to be logged in - and do the install.

Confirm step (both paths): message the user to check that the app opens. Once they confirm, close the ticket. If they don't reply within 2 business days, the ticket auto-closes, nothing for you to do.
stages: Receive software request ticket from the portal
Check the requested title against the Approved Software List
Send manager approval request from the ticket
Reassign ticket to the Security queue for review
Log the license with Procurement using the cost center from the approval form
Schedule a remote session with the logged-in user
Install the software during the remote session (or push from the deployment console for ASL items)
Ask the user to confirm the app opens
Close the ticket

decisions.question: Is the requested software on the Approved Software List?
branches: Yes: push from the deployment console, tag 'ASL-push', go to the confirm step
No: request manager approval, then security review

decisions.question: What is the manager's response to the approval request?
branches: Approves: reassign ticket to the Security queue
Declines: close ticket and paste the reason into the user-facing note
No response in 3 business days: send one reminder and wait 2 more business days; if still no response, close as 'Expired - no approval' and tell user they can resubmit

decisions.question: What is Security's review outcome?
branches: Cleared: log license with Procurement, schedule remote session, install
Rejected: close ticket and copy Security's note to the user
Use alternative: offer the named ASL equivalent; if user accepts, handle as ASL push; if user declines, close as rejected

edge_cases: Manager approval timeout: after 3 business days with no response, one reminder is sent with 2 more business days allowed; if still unanswered, the ticket closes as 'Expired - no approval' and the user may resubmit.
Security suggests an ASL alternative: the request loops back to the ASL path (console push, ASL-push tag) if the user accepts, or closes as rejected if not.
User doesn't reply to the confirmation message within 2 business days: the ticket auto-closes.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a user requests software not on the ASL and the manager never responds, even after the reminder?
trace_questions.answer: After 3 business days with no response, one reminder is sent and 2 more business days are given. If there is still no answer, the ticket is closed as 'Expired - no approval' and the user is told they can resubmit.

trace_questions.question: What happens if the manager approves a non-ASL request, Security responds with 'use alternative', and the user accepts the suggested equivalent?
trace_questions.answer: The request is handled like an ASL request: the alternative is pushed from the deployment console and the ticket is tagged 'ASL-push'. The user is then asked to confirm the app opens, and the ticket is closed once they confirm, or auto-closes if they don't reply within 2 business days.

title: Intern Relocation Stipend Requests at Summit Ridge Manufacturing
workflow_text:
Relocation stipend - how I handle these (for whoever covers while I'm out in July)

Quick version: intern puts in the request on the HR portal, we check it, manager signs, sometimes Finance, intern signs the repayment form, payroll pays it. Details below, sorry it's a bit all over the place.

FIRST THING when a request lands in the queue: check the home address on the form against the site address. Policy is 50+ miles one way. Under 50 = not eligible. Send the 'Relocation - Not Eligible' template from the shared mailbox and close it out in the tracker. Don't bother reviewing docs on those. Fully remote interns also go straight to the not-eligible template, no distance check needed (they sometimes apply anyway).

If they're eligible, go through the attachments. Need: signed lease or housing agreement covering the internship dates + proof of first payment/deposit. If anything's missing, unsigned, or unreadable -> kick it back to the intern through the portal with a note saying exactly what's missing. Then it just sits until they re-upload, and you review the new upload the same way (yes, sometimes this goes 2-3 rounds).
  - IMPORTANT: if they haven't re-uploaded within 5 business days of you kicking it back, close the request as 'Incomplete' in the tracker. They get ONE resubmission after that, it comes in as a fresh request and starts over at the distance check.

Once docs are good, work out the amount. Standard is flat $1,500.
  - Most people just get the $1,500, move on.
  - Some ask for more (high-cost-of-living areas, usually the downtown office). If the request is over $1,500 it has to go to Finance AFTER the manager signs, not before.
     * Finance approves the higher amount -> use their approved number.
     * Finance declines -> drop it back to the standard $1,500 and keep going. Don't ask the intern, just note it in the confirmation email later.

Manager sign-off: send the approval form to the intern's hiring manager. Usually quick. If no response in 3 business days, escalate to the department head and they can sign instead. If the manager (or dept head) actually rejects it, request is denied - email the intern with the reason they gave and close in tracker.

After all approvals: intern has to e-sign the repayment agreement (if they leave before week 6 they pay back the whole stipend - HR handles the clawback, not us). Don't send anything to payroll until that's signed.

Then submit to payroll. Cutoff is Wednesday noon - if it's in before that, it goes on this Friday's check. After cutoff = next pay cycle. 

Last bits: confirmation email to the intern with the amount + which paycheck it lands on (and mention if Finance capped it), then update the tracker to 'Paid/Scheduled'.
stages: Receive relocation stipend request from intern via HR portal
Check eligibility based on home-to-site distance (and remote status)
Review attached lease/housing agreement and proof of payment
Calculate stipend amount (standard $1,500 or requested higher amount)
Send approval form to hiring manager for sign-off
Send above-standard requests to Finance for review
Have intern e-sign the repayment agreement
Submit stipend to payroll
Send confirmation email to intern with amount and pay date
Update tracker to 'Paid/Scheduled'

decisions.question: Is the intern eligible (home address 50+ miles from site and not fully remote)?
branches: Yes: proceed to document review
No (under 50 miles or fully remote): send 'Relocation - Not Eligible' template and close in tracker

decisions.question: Are the documents complete, signed, and readable?
branches: Yes: proceed to calculate amount
No: send back to intern via portal with note on what's missing; review re-upload again (loop)

decisions.question: Is the requested amount over the standard $1,500?
branches: No: use $1,500 and continue to manager sign-off
Yes: after manager sign-off, send to Finance (nested decision below)

decisions.question: (Nested) Does Finance approve the higher amount?
branches: Yes: use Finance's approved amount
No: reduce to standard $1,500, continue without asking intern, and note it in confirmation email

decisions.question: Does the hiring manager (or department head) approve?
branches: Yes: continue (to Finance if over $1,500, otherwise to repayment agreement)
No: deny request, email intern with reason, close in tracker

decisions.question: Was the request submitted to payroll before the Wednesday noon cutoff?
branches: Yes: paid on this Friday's check
No: paid on next pay cycle

edge_cases: If the intern doesn't re-upload missing documents within 5 business days, the request is closed as 'Incomplete'; the intern gets one resubmission, which starts over at the distance check.
If the hiring manager doesn't respond within 3 business days, escalate to the department head, who can sign instead.
If the intern leaves before week 6, they must repay the full stipend under the repayment agreement (clawback handled by HR); nothing goes to payroll until that agreement is signed.

trace_questions.question: What happens if an intern living 80 miles away submits complete documents requesting $2,200, the manager approves, but Finance declines the higher amount?
trace_questions.answer: The stipend drops to the standard $1,500 without asking the intern. The intern then e-signs the repayment agreement, it's submitted to payroll (this Friday if before Wednesday noon, otherwise next cycle), and the confirmation email states the $1,500 amount, notes Finance capped it, and gives the pay date; tracker is updated to 'Paid/Scheduled'.

trace_questions.question: What happens if an eligible intern's lease is unsigned, the request is kicked back, and the intern doesn't re-upload within 5 business days?
trace_questions.answer: The request is closed as 'Incomplete' in the tracker. The intern may resubmit once; the resubmission comes in as a fresh request and starts over at the distance/eligibility check.

title: Responding to a Credential Leaked in a Code Repository
workflow_text:
Leaked secret alerts – how we work them (for whoever's on SecOps rotation)

Alerts come in from the repo scanner (Northgate's code host flags anything that looks like an API key, token, password string etc.). They land in the SecOps queue and auto-create a ticket, so you don't need to make one.

First thing: open the alert and look at the actual string + file. Lots of these are junk – sample configs, unit test fixtures, "AKIA_EXAMPLE" style placeholders. Try to validate it: for cloud keys run the read-only identity check from the jump box, for internal service tokens hit the token introspection endpoint. If it's dead/fake -> mark false positive, add a one-liner on why, close. Done.

If it's live, look it up in the secrets inventory to find who owns it (team + named contact).
- Can't find it in inventory? Happens with old stuff. Check git blame on the commit and ask that person / their manager. If still nobody claims it by end of day, we treat SecOps as owner and proceed.

Next thing that matters is WHERE it leaked:
- Public repo (anything on the public org, or a fork that went public): assume it's already been scraped. Revoke/rotate NOW. Don't wait to hear back from the owner – just ping them so they know their service may break.
- Internal-only repo: message the owner and give them the chance to rotate themselves so they can coordinate the deploy. They have 24h. No response in 24h -> we rotate it ourselves.

After rotation, the owner needs to get the secret scrubbed from repo history (not just a new commit deleting it – history rewrite). Put the request in the ticket and assign that subtask to them.

If rotating breaks a prod service, DO NOT restore the old key. Get the owner to push the new one into their config/vault. Old key stays dead.

Then pull the access logs for that key from the commit timestamp up to revocation. Look for source IPs/regions/user agents that aren't the owning service.
- Anything unrecognized -> escalate to Incident Response (page the IR on-call, link the ticket). They own it from there; leave your ticket open and linked.
- All usage looks like the owning service -> write up what you found (owner, exposure type, when rotated, log review result) and close.
stages: Open the alert and review the flagged string and file
Validate whether the credential is live
Look up the credential owner in the secrets inventory
Notify the owner
Revoke and rotate the credential
Assign the owner to purge the secret from repo history
Review the key's access logs from commit time to revocation
Document findings and close the ticket

decisions.question: Is the flagged credential live/valid?
branches: No (dead, fake, placeholder, or test fixture): mark as false positive with a brief reason and close the ticket
Yes: continue by looking up the owner in the secrets inventory

decisions.question: Was the credential leaked in a public repo or an internal-only repo?
branches: Public repo (including a fork that went public): revoke/rotate immediately without waiting for the owner, and ping the owner to warn of possible breakage
Internal-only repo: notify the owner and give them 24 hours to rotate it themselves

decisions.question: Does the access log review show any unrecognized usage of the key?
branches: Yes: escalate to Incident Response by paging the IR on-call and linking the ticket; IR takes ownership and the SecOps ticket stays open and linked
No (all usage matches the owning service): document owner, exposure type, rotation time, and log review result, then close

edge_cases: Owner not found in the secrets inventory: check git blame and ask the committer or their manager; if no one claims it by end of day, SecOps becomes the owner and proceeds. Similarly, if an internal-repo owner doesn't respond within 24 hours, SecOps rotates the credential itself.
Rotation breaks a production service: do not restore the old key; the owner must deploy the new key into their config/vault while the old key stays revoked.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a live service token is found in an internal-only repo, the owner never responds, and the later log review shows calls from an unfamiliar region?
trace_questions.answer: The owner is given 24 hours to rotate; with no response, SecOps rotates the token itself. After assigning the history purge, SecOps reviews the logs, and because of the unrecognized region it pages the IR on-call and links the ticket. IR takes ownership and the SecOps ticket stays open and linked rather than being closed.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a valid cloud key is found on a public repo and rotating it immediately takes down the owner's production service?
trace_questions.answer: Because it is public, SecOps revokes/rotates right away without waiting for the owner and pings them. When prod breaks, the old key is not restored; the owner must push the new key into their config/vault. The owner is then assigned the repo history purge, and SecOps reviews access logs from commit time to revocation, escalating to IR if anything is unrecognized or documenting and closing if all usage is from the owning service.

title: Lost or Stolen Mobile Device with Company Access
workflow_text:
Lost/stolen phone calls - notes for whoever's covering the desk

First thing: DON'T wipe anything until you know who you're talking to. Log the ticket (category Mobile > Lost/Stolen) and verify the caller. Call back on the number in the HR directory, NOT the number they're calling from (obviously, they don't have their phone). If callback doesn't work, get their manager to confirm by Teams/email. If you can't get either one, just disable the account sign-in and leave the ticket in Pending Verification. No wipe, no MFA changes until somebody confirms.

Once verified -> kill their sessions right away. Revoke all sign-in sessions + force a password reset in the admin portal. Do this before anything else, even before the MDM lookup.

Then pull up the device in MDM and check the ownership field.
- Corp-owned: we do a full wipe.
- BYOD: selective wipe ONLY (removes the work profile/managed apps). We do not full-wipe personal phones, ever, even if the user asks. Tell them to use their own phone provider's find/erase tool for the rest.

Ask whether it's lost or stolen, it matters:
* Stolen -> send the wipe now.
* Lost (left it in a cab, can't find it at home, etc.) -> put it in Lost Mode first (locks it, shows our desk number on the screen). User gets 24 hrs to find it. If they find it, unlock, note it in the ticket, close. If 24 hrs pass and it's still missing, send the wipe like normal.

After you send the wipe, watch for the confirmation in MDM. No confirmation = resend every 4 hrs (phone might be off/no signal). If you hit 72 hrs with no confirmation, stop resending, escalate to Security, mark the device "Unconfirmed Wipe" in the asset record. Security will revoke the device certificate on their side.

Corp-owned only: once the wipe is sent, call the carrier to suspend the line. BYOD = their line, their problem.

Replacement (corp-owned only): order through procurement. If it was stolen we need the police report number in the ticket before you place the order - no number, no order, ticket waits. Lost devices don't need a report.

MFA: re-enroll them on the new/temp device. Use a temporary access pass if they have nothing else. Do this after the wipe has been sent, not before.

Oh - also check their groups. If they're in Finance, HR, or anything tagged Restricted, open a ticket in the Security incident queue too, regardless of lost/stolen. Everyone else, skip it.

If a device turns up AFTER the wipe went out, it still counts as wiped. Have them bring it to the desk to re-enroll it, don't try to undo anything remotely.

Last step: update the asset record (status Lost, Stolen, Wiped, etc.) and close the ticket.
stages: Log the ticket under Mobile > Lost/Stolen
Verify the caller's identity via callback to the directory number or manager confirmation
Revoke all sign-in sessions and force a password reset
Look up the device in MDM and check the ownership field
Place the device in Lost Mode and give the user 24 hours to find it (lost devices only)
Send the wipe command (full wipe for corp-owned, selective wipe for BYOD)
Monitor MDM for wipe confirmation, resending every 4 hours
Call the carrier to suspend the line (corp-owned only)
Order a replacement device through procurement (corp-owned only)
Re-enroll MFA on the new or temporary device, using a temporary access pass if needed
Check group membership and open a Security incident ticket if the user has restricted access
Update the asset record status and close the ticket

decisions.question: Can the caller's identity be verified?
branches: Callback to HR directory number succeeds: proceed with session revocation and the rest of the process
Callback fails but manager confirms by Teams/email: proceed with the process
Neither works: disable account sign-in only, set ticket to Pending Verification, no wipe or MFA changes

decisions.question: Is the device corp-owned or BYOD?
branches: Corp-owned: full wipe, carrier suspension, and replacement ordered through procurement
BYOD: selective wipe of work profile only (never a full wipe, even on request); user handles their own line and uses their provider's erase tool

decisions.question: Was the device lost or stolen?
branches: Stolen: send the wipe immediately; police report number required before ordering a replacement
Lost: put in Lost Mode and wait 24 hours (nested decision on whether it is found)

decisions.question: (Lost devices) Was the device found within 24 hours?
branches: Found: unlock it, note it in the ticket, close the ticket
Not found after 24 hours: send the wipe as normal

decisions.question: Has wipe confirmation been received in MDM?
branches: Confirmed: continue with remaining steps
Not confirmed: resend every 4 hours; after 72 hours stop resending, escalate to Security, mark asset 'Unconfirmed Wipe', and Security revokes the device certificate

decisions.question: Is the user in Finance, HR, or a Restricted-tagged group?
branches: Yes: open a ticket in the Security incident queue regardless of lost/stolen
No: skip the Security ticket

edge_cases: Caller cannot be verified by callback or manager: only disable sign-in and hold ticket in Pending Verification with no wipe or MFA changes
Wipe never confirms: resend loop every 4 hours until 72 hours, then escalate to Security, mark 'Unconfirmed Wipe', and Security revokes the device certificate
Device is found after the wipe was already sent: it still counts as wiped and the user must bring it to the desk to re-enroll rather than undoing anything remotely
Stolen corp-owned device with no police report number: replacement order is held and the ticket waits

trace_questions.question: What happens if a verified user reports their BYOD phone as lost (not stolen), they are not in any restricted group, and they still haven't found it after 24 hours?
trace_questions.answer: After sessions are revoked and the password reset, the phone is placed in Lost Mode for 24 hours. When it's still missing, a selective wipe (work profile only) is sent and monitored for confirmation. No carrier suspension or replacement order is done by the desk since it's BYOD; MFA is re-enrolled on their new/temp device after the wipe is sent, no Security incident ticket is opened, and the asset record is updated and the ticket closed.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a corp-owned phone is reported stolen by a verified HR employee and the wipe still hasn't confirmed after 72 hours?
trace_questions.answer: Sessions are revoked and the password reset, then a full wipe is sent immediately and the carrier is called to suspend the line. The wipe is resent every 4 hours; at 72 hours resending stops, the issue is escalated to Security, the asset is marked 'Unconfirmed Wipe', and Security revokes the device certificate. Because the user is in HR, a Security incident queue ticket is also opened. A replacement is ordered only once the police report number is in the ticket, and MFA is re-enrolled on the new/temp device.

title: Emergency Student Hardship Grant Requests
workflow_text:
Hardship fund notes, for whoever covers the inbox while I'm out.

Apps come in through the Student Support portal and land in the Hardship queue. Pull the oldest one first unless something is flagged URGENT (see the bottom of this note).

First thing: look the student up in the records system. They have to be enrolled at least half-time THIS term. If they're not, it's a denial. Use the denial template, which has the appeal info and a link to the off-campus resources list. Don't spend time on docs or anything else for these.

Then open the fund tracker spreadsheet and search their ID for any award earlier in this academic year.
- no prior award -> normal routing (below)
- prior award -> it goes to the Dean of Students director for sign-off NO MATTER the amount. Combined awards for the year are capped at $1,500, so if they got $1,000 in fall the most the director can approve now is $500. Put the prior amount at the top of the case summary so the director sees it.

Docs: we need a short statement plus proof of the expense (bill, lease notice, repair quote, etc.). If something's missing, email the student and give them 5 business days. If nothing comes back, send ONE reminder and give them 3 more business days. Still nothing = close the case as incomplete and log it. They can reapply whenever; they just start over. If they send docs but they're still not enough, ask again. Same clock rules apply.

Routing, once docs are complete. Write the one-paragraph case summary, then:
- $750 or less (and no prior award): you can approve it yourself as coordinator.
- over $750: goes to the committee, which meets Tuesdays. The committee comes back with full approval, partial (they set the amount), or deny. A deny gets the same denial template as above.

After anything is approved, BEFORE you tell the student, send the approved amount to Financial Aid so they can check it against cost of attendance. Usually they say fine. If the grant would push the student over COA, FA gives us the max allowed and we cut the award down to that number. Don't argue with them.

Then send the award email (template in the shared drive), and after that fill out the disbursement form for the Bursar.

re: Bursar. If the student owes a balance on their account, the Bursar applies the grant to the balance first, and anything left over goes to them as a refund by direct deposit. EXCEPTION: if the application is tagged as a housing or food emergency, check the "direct to student" box on the form. Then the Bursar skips the balance and deposits the whole thing. No balance = straight direct deposit, nothing to check.

Last step on every case (approved, denied, or incomplete): log the outcome and amount in the fund tracker and mark the case closed in the portal.

URGENT ones: eviction notice or utility shutoff within 72 hours. You still have to confirm enrollment, but you can approve up to $300 the same day before docs come in and send it straight to the Bursar form. Collect docs afterward. If they asked for more than $300, the rest goes through the normal routing once docs are in.
stages: Pull the next application from the portal Hardship queue
Verify half-time or greater enrollment in the records system
Check the fund tracker for prior awards this academic year
Review the submitted documents for completeness
Email the student to request missing documents
Write the case summary and route it for approval
Obtain the approval decision from the coordinator, committee, or director
Send the approved amount to Financial Aid for the cost-of-attendance check
Send the award email to the student
Submit the disbursement form to the Bursar
Send the denial email with appeal information and resources (denial path)
Log the outcome in the fund tracker and close the case in the portal

decisions.question: Is the student enrolled at least half-time this term?
branches: Yes: continue to the prior-award check
No: send the denial template with appeal info and off-campus resources, log, and close

decisions.question: Has the student already received an award this academic year?
branches: No: normal amount-based routing
Yes: director sign-off is required regardless of amount, and the combined yearly total is capped at $1,500

decisions.question: Are the documents (statement plus proof of expense) complete?
branches: Yes: write the case summary and route for approval

No: email the student with a 5-business-day deadline. If there is no response, send one reminder with 3 more business days. If there is still no response, close as incomplete. If the docs come back still insufficient, request again under the same clock (loop)

decisions.question: Is the requested amount $750 or less (with no prior award)?
branches: Yes: the coordinator approves it directly
No: send to the Tuesday committee, which decides full approval, partial approval at an amount it sets, or denial (denial uses the denial template)

decisions.question: Does the student owe a balance on their account?
branches: No: the Bursar sends the full grant by direct deposit
Yes, and the application is tagged housing or food emergency: check 'direct to student' so the Bursar deposits the full amount and skips the balance
Yes, not tagged housing or food: the Bursar applies the grant to the balance first and refunds any remainder by direct deposit

edge_cases: Urgent cases (eviction notice or utility shutoff within 72 hours): after confirming enrollment, the coordinator may approve up to $300 the same day before docs arrive and send it directly to the Bursar form. Docs are collected afterward, and any amount requested above $300 goes through normal routing once docs are in.

Documentation timeout: no response within 5 business days, then one reminder and 3 more business days with no response, means the case is closed as incomplete and logged. The student may reapply but starts over.
Cost-of-attendance limit: if Financial Aid says the grant would push the student over COA, the award is reduced to the maximum FA provides before the student is notified.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a half-time student with no prior award requests $1,200, initially leaves out proof of expense but sends it after the first email, the committee approves a partial $800, FA clears it, and the student owes a balance on a request not tagged housing or food?
trace_questions.answer: After the docs arrive, the coordinator writes the case summary. Because $1,200 is over $750, it goes to the Tuesday committee, which sets a partial award of $800. The $800 goes to Financial Aid for the COA check, which clears. The student gets the award email, and then the Bursar disbursement form is submitted without the 'direct to student' box. The Bursar applies the $800 to the outstanding balance first and refunds any remainder by direct deposit. The outcome is logged in the tracker and the case is closed.

trace_questions.question: What happens if an enrolled student who received $1,000 earlier this year submits complete docs requesting $700 for a housing emergency and also owes a balance on their account?
trace_questions.answer: Because of the prior award, the case goes to the director for sign-off regardless of amount. The $1,500 yearly cap means the director can approve at most $500. The approved amount goes to Financial Aid for the COA check before the student is notified. The award email is then sent, and the Bursar form is submitted with 'direct to student' checked because the request is tagged housing. The Bursar deposits the full grant to the student instead of applying it to the balance. Finally, the case is logged and closed.

title: Enrollment Verification Letter Requests at the Registrar's Office
workflow_text:
Enrollment verification letters - how we handle them (for front desk / student workers)

Requests come in through the online Verification Request form on the Registrar page. They land in the shared inbox (registrar-verify@). Work them oldest first.

1st thing: pull up the student in the student info system using the student ID number on the form. Make sure name + DOB on the form match the record.
- If the ID number is missing or doesn't match anyone, don't guess. Email the student asking for their correct ID, and move the request to the "Waiting on Student" folder. If we hear nothing back in 5 business days, close it out and send the standard "request closed - please resubmit" email.

Once you've got the right record, check enrollment for the term they asked about.
- Not enrolled for that term (no registered credits) -> we can't issue the letter. Send the "Not Enrolled" template email and close the request. Done.
- Enrolled -> keep going.

Generate the letter from the Enrollment Verification template in the doc system. It auto-fills name, term, credit load (FT/PT), and expected grad date. Double check the term is right before saving.

Print & bring to the Assistant Registrar for signature + office seal. (They usually sign in batches at 11 and 3.)

Delivery - check what the student picked on the form:
- Email/PDF: scan the signed letter, send as PDF to the student's university email only (not personal addresses).
- Mailed paper copy: put it in a university envelope, address to whatever mailing address is on the form, drop in outgoing mail bin.

Last step: log it in the Verification Tracker spreadsheet (date, student ID, term, delivery method, your initials) and move the email to "Completed."
stages: Receive the request from the online Verification Request form in the shared inbox
Look up the student's record by student ID and confirm name and date of birth match
Check the student's enrollment for the requested term
Generate the letter from the Enrollment Verification template and verify the term
Obtain the Assistant Registrar's signature and office seal
Deliver the letter by the method the student selected
Log the request in the Verification Tracker and move the email to Completed

decisions.question: Is the student enrolled (has registered credits) for the requested term?
branches: No: send the "Not Enrolled" template email and close the request
Yes: continue to generate the verification letter

decisions.question: Which delivery method did the student select on the form?
branches: Email/PDF: scan the signed letter and send it as a PDF to the student's university email only
Mailed paper copy: place it in a university envelope addressed to the mailing address on the form and put it in the outgoing mail bin

edge_cases: If the student ID is missing or doesn't match a record, email the student for the correct ID and move the request to "Waiting on Student"; if there is no reply within 5 business days, close it and send the "request closed - please resubmit" email.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a student submits a request with a valid student ID, is registered for the requested term, and selects email delivery but lists a personal email address?
trace_questions.answer: The record is confirmed, enrollment is verified, the letter is generated, signed and sealed by the Assistant Registrar, then scanned and sent as a PDF to the student's university email only (not the personal address). The request is then logged in the Verification Tracker and moved to Completed.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a request has a student ID that doesn't match anyone, and the student replies two days later with the correct ID but turns out to have no registered credits for the requested term?
trace_questions.answer: The request first goes to "Waiting on Student" after emailing for the correct ID. Since the student replied within 5 business days, the record is looked up with the correct ID; the enrollment check shows no registered credits, so the "Not Enrolled" template email is sent and the request is closed without a letter.

title: Processing a Firewall Rule Change Request
workflow_text:
Firewall change reqs - how I work them (for whoever's covering while I'm out)

Everything comes in thru the FW-Changes queue in the ticket tool. Grab the oldest first unless it's tagged EMERGENCY (see bottom).

First thing: is the form actually filled out? Need src, dest, port/proto, business justification, and a named system owner. If anything's missing, kick it back to the requester w/ a note saying what's missing and set status to Waiting on Requester. When they resubmit it goes back to the top of this process, check it all again, don't assume they fixed everything. If they don't reply in 5 business days the ticket auto-closes as Abandoned, nothing for you to do.

Expiry field - people leave it blank constantly. That's fine, don't bounce it for that, just default it to 90 days.

Any/any requests (any src to any dest, or any port) = reject outright, don't even score them. Close w/ the standard 'not permitted by policy' reply.

If the dest is internal you skip straight to scoring. If it's external (internet), look the IP/domain up in the threat intel blocklist first. On the blocklist -> reject, close the ticket, tell the requester why, and also drop a note to the SOC channel so they know someone was trying to reach a bad host. Not on the list -> go on to scoring.

Scoring = the risk sheet in the team drive. Score under 7, you can approve it yourself. 7 or above goes to the security architect. Architect will do one of three things:
- approve -> carry on
- deny -> close the ticket, architect's reason goes in the reply to the requester
- request changes (usually 'narrow the port range' or 'use a specific src subnet not a /16') -> send it back to the requester like an incomplete form; when it comes back it starts over from the completeness check and gets re-scored

Once approved, schedule it in the next change window (Tue or Thu nights). Then on the night: stage the rule in the policy manager, push it, and run a connectivity test with the requester on a call.

Test fails -> roll back right away, check w/ network team what went wrong, fix and retry ONCE. If the retry also fails, roll back again, mark the ticket Failed Implementation and escalate to the network eng lead. Requester gets told it's escalated. Don't close it.

Test passes -> tag the rule in the policy manager with the ticket # and expiry date, then notify requester and close.

EMERGENCY: if it's tagged emergency AND a manager approved the tag in the ticket, you skip the change window and implement right away (still do the blocklist check + scoring + architect if 7+, no shortcuts there). Everything after is the same - test, tag, close. BUT you have to file a retroactive CAB record within 24 hrs. If CAB rejects it retroactively, the rule gets pulled.
stages: Pick up the request ticket from the FW-Changes queue
Check the form for required fields (src, dest, port/proto, justification, system owner)
Check an external destination against the threat intel blocklist
Score the request using the risk sheet
Send high-risk requests to the security architect for review
Schedule the change in the next Tue/Thu change window
Stage the rule in the policy manager and push it
Run a connectivity test with the requester
Tag the rule with the ticket number and expiry date
Notify the requester and close the ticket
File a retroactive CAB record within 24 hours (emergency changes)

decisions.question: Is the request form complete (src, dest, port/proto, justification, system owner)?
branches: Yes: continue processing
No: send back to requester as Waiting on Requester; on resubmission restart at the completeness check; no reply in 5 business days auto-closes as Abandoned

decisions.question: Is the destination external, and if so, is it on the threat intel blocklist?
branches: Internal: skip straight to risk scoring
External and on the blocklist: reject, close the ticket, tell the requester why, and notify the SOC channel
External and not on the blocklist: proceed to risk scoring

decisions.question: Is the risk score 7 or higher, and if so what does the security architect decide?
branches: Under 7: analyst approves it
7+ and architect approves: proceed to implementation
7+ and architect denies: close the ticket with the architect's reason sent to the requester
7+ and architect requests changes: send back to requester; resubmission restarts at the completeness check and is re-scored

decisions.question: Is the request tagged emergency with manager approval?
branches: Yes: skip the change window and implement immediately, then file a retroactive CAB record within 24 hours
No: schedule in the next Tue/Thu change window

decisions.question: Does the connectivity test pass?
branches: Yes: tag the rule with ticket # and expiry, notify requester, close
No (first failure): roll back, check with the network team, fix and retry once
No (retry also fails): roll back, mark Failed Implementation, escalate to network eng lead, notify requester, leave ticket open

edge_cases: Any/any requests (any source to any destination, or any port) are rejected outright without scoring
A blank expiry field is not grounds for rejection; it defaults to 90 days
Requester doesn't respond within 5 business days after being sent back: ticket auto-closes as Abandoned
Emergency change rejected retroactively by CAB: the rule is pulled

trace_questions.question: What happens if a non-emergency request to an external IP not on the blocklist scores 8, the architect approves it, but the connectivity test fails on the first try and again on the retry?
trace_questions.answer: It is scheduled in the next Tue/Thu change window and pushed. After the first failed test the rule is rolled back, the analyst checks with the network team, fixes it and retries once. When the retry also fails, it is rolled back again, the ticket is marked Failed Implementation, escalated to the network eng lead, and the requester is told it's escalated. The ticket is not closed.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a manager-approved emergency request to an internal destination scores 4, passes its connectivity test, but CAB later rejects the retroactive record?
trace_questions.answer: The blocklist check is skipped because the destination is internal; the score under 7 means the analyst approves without the architect. It is implemented immediately outside the change window, the test passes, the rule is tagged with the ticket # and expiry (90 days if left blank), and the requester is notified and the ticket closed. A retroactive CAB record is filed within 24 hours; because CAB rejects it, the rule gets pulled.

title: Mailbox Full / Quota Increase Requests
workflow_text:
Notes for handling "my mailbox is full" tickets. These come in a lot near quarter-end.

When one comes in, log it in the queue under Email > Quota. Make sure the user's name, dept and email address are on the ticket. Some people submit from a personal phone, so double-check.

Next, pull up the user's mailbox in the admin console and check current usage against the 50 GB cap. Screenshot the usage panel and attach it to the ticket. We need this later if it goes to Messaging.

If they're under 90%, we don't do anything on the back end. Reply with the standard cleanup guide (KB-0412: empty Deleted Items, clear big attachments, set up auto-archive rules) and resolve the ticket. Most of these are people seeing the 'approaching limit' warning early.

If they're at 90% or higher, reach out and book a 15-min remote session to turn on online archive. This moves anything older than 2 yrs out of the main mailbox.
  - If the user doesn't answer within 3 business days, send one reminder. If there's still nothing 2 business days after the reminder, close the ticket as "No response – user may reopen."

During the session, enable online archive with the user on the line. Show them where the Archive folder lives so they don't panic when old mail "disappears."

Wait 24 hrs for the archive move to finish, then recheck usage in the console. Take a second screenshot.

After the recheck:
- Below 90% now? Good. Skip escalation.
- Still 90%+? Escalate to the Messaging team (Tier 2) for a quota bump to the 100 GB tier. Reassign the ticket to their queue and attach both screenshots (before/after). They'll assign it back to us when the change is done.

Last step either way: message the user to confirm things look OK on their end, then close the ticket.
stages: Log the ticket under Email > Quota with the user's name, department, and email
Check mailbox usage in the admin console and attach a screenshot
Contact the user to book a remote session
Enable online archive with the user during the session
Wait 24 hours and recheck usage, attaching a second screenshot
Escalate to the Messaging team for a quota increase to 100 GB
Confirm with the user and close the ticket

decisions.question: Is the user's mailbox usage at 90% or more of the 50 GB cap?
branches: Below 90%: reply with the cleanup guide (KB-0412) and resolve the ticket with no back-end changes
90% or higher: contact the user to book a 15-minute remote session to enable online archive

decisions.question: After the 24-hour recheck, is usage still at 90% or more?
branches: Below 90%: skip escalation, confirm with the user, and close the ticket
Still 90% or higher: reassign to the Messaging team with both screenshots for a bump to the 100 GB tier; when they assign it back, confirm with the user and close

edge_cases: User does not respond to the session request within 3 business days: send one reminder; if there is still no reply 2 business days after the reminder, close the ticket as "No response – user may reopen."

trace_questions.question: What happens if a user's mailbox is at 85% of the cap when the ticket is checked?
trace_questions.answer: No back-end change is made. The tech replies with the standard cleanup guide (KB-0412) and resolves the ticket. No archive session is booked.

trace_questions.question: What happens if a user is at 96%, online archive is enabled, and the recheck 24 hours later shows 93%?
trace_questions.answer: Usage is still at 90% or higher, so the ticket is escalated. It is reassigned to the Messaging team's queue with the before and after screenshots attached, for a bump to the 100 GB tier. When Messaging assigns it back, the tech confirms with the user and closes the ticket.
